story.fix: Create ClusterRole node-reader (get,list nodes) and ClusterRoleBinding node-viewer-binding to node-viewer.

questions.title: Helm template (Argo CD without CRDs)

pic.say: Render a Helm chart to YAML without installing CRDs.

questions.words:
• Helm = a tool that installs packaged applications into Kubernetes.
  • Chart = the package. It lives in a repo (a URL). A chart has values = settings you can switch.
  • helm template = print the YAML the chart WOULD create. Nothing is installed. (helm install is the command that really installs.)

questions.title: Helm install, upgrade, rollback

pic.say: Install, upgrade and roll back an app with Helm.

questions.words:
• Release = one installed copy of a chart. It has a name and lives in a namespace.
  • Revision = the version number of a release. Install = revision 1. Every upgrade or rollback adds 1.
  • --set name=value = change one of the chart's settings on the command line.
questions.setup:
helm version || curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helm/helm/main/scripts/get-helm-3 | bash
helm uninstall web -n demo 2>/dev/null
k delete ns demo --ignore-not-found
helm repo remove ingress-nginx 2>/dev/null
questions.question: 1. Add the Helm repository `https://kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx` with the name `ingress-nginx`.
questions.meaning: Install with one setting. Change that setting. Undo the change. You need the exact name of the "replicas" setting; helm show values gives it.

steps.title: Step 1. Add the repo
steps.html:
helm repo add ingress-nginx https://kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx
helm repo update

steps.title: Step 2. Find the setting name
steps.html:
helm show values ingress-nginx/ingress-nginx | grep -n replicaCount

You see replicaCount: 1, indented under controller:. So the setting name is controller.replicaCount.

flow.t: helm show values ingress-nginx/ingress-nginx | grep -n replicaCount

flow.h: You see replicaCount: 1, indented under controller:. So the setting name is controller.replicaCount.

steps.title: Step 3. Install
steps.html:
helm install web ingress-nginx/ingress-nginx -n demo --create-namespace --set controller.replicaCount=2

Reading it: helm install <release> <repo>/<chart> -n <namespace>. --create-namespace makes the namespace if it does not exist.

flow.t: helm install web ingress-nginx/ingress-nginx -n demo --create-namespace --set controller.replicaCount=2

steps.html: helm upgrade web ingress-nginx/ingress-nginx -n demo --set controller.replicaCount=3

helm history web -n demo

You see revision 1 (superseded) and revision 2 (deployed).

You want STATUS deployed, REVISION 3 (the rollback is itself a new revision).

questions.title: Kustomize

pic.say: Apply a Kustomize folder.

questions.words:
• Kustomize = a way to take a normal YAML file and apply changes to it without editing that file. It is built into kubectl.
  • kustomization.yaml = the file that lists which YAML files to use (resources:) and what to change (namespace, replicas, image...).
  • -k <folder> = tell kubectl to read a folder that contains a kustomization.yaml. (-f is for a normal file.)
questions.setup:
k delete ns kust --ignore-not-found
rm -rf /root/kust && mkdir -p /root/kust && cd /root/kust
k create deploy kweb --image=nginx:1.27 --dry-run=client -o yaml > deploy.yaml
cat > kustomization.yaml <<EOF
resources:
- deploy.yaml
namespace: kust
replicas:
- name: kweb
  count: 2
EOF
k create ns kust
cd ; clear
questions.question: A Kustomize configuration exists in `/root/kust`. Change it so that deployment `kweb` runs with `3` replicas, then apply it. Do not edit `deploy.yaml`.
questions.meaning: The change goes into kustomization.yaml, not into the base file. Then apply the FOLDER with -k.

steps.title: Step 1. Read what is there
steps.html:
ls /root/kust
cat /root/kust/kustomization.yaml

You see:

resources:
- deploy.yaml
namespace: kust
replicas:
- name: kweb
  count: 2

How it reads: "Take deploy.yaml. Put everything in namespace kust. Set kweb to 2 replicas."

flow.h: You see:

flow.t:
resources:
- deploy.yaml
namespace: kust
replicas:
- name: kweb
  count: 2

flow.h: How it reads: "Take deploy.yaml. Put everything in namespace kust. Set kweb to 2 replicas."

steps.title: Step 2. Make the change
steps.html:
vim /root/kust/kustomization.yaml

Change count: 2 to count: 3. Save with Esc, :wq.

flow.h: Change count: 2 to count: 3. Save with Esc, :wq.

steps.title: Step 3. Preview (creates nothing)
steps.html:
k kustomize /root/kust

It prints the final YAML. Check that you see replicas: 3 and namespace: kust.

flow.h: It prints the final YAML. Check that you see replicas: 3 and namespace: kust.

steps.title: Step 4. Apply the folder
steps.html: k apply -k /root/kust

steps.title: Closing routine
steps.html:
k get deploy -n kust

You want kweb 3/3.

exit          # exam only

flow.h: You want kweb 3/3.

You see Cause Fix
error: ... must be a directory or a parse error you used -f with the folder use -k
No resources found in k get deploy you looked in the wrong namespace. The kustomization sets it. read namespace: in the file
the question asks for a new image tag instead different block add to kustomization.yaml: images: / - name: nginx / newTag: "1.28"

questions.title: cri-dockerd (prepare a node)

• Container runtime = the program on a node that actually runs containers. cri-dockerd is an adapter that lets Kubernetes use Docker as that runtime.
  • .deb file = an installer package for Debian/Ubuntu. dpkg -i <file> installs it.
  • sysctl = a Linux kernel setting, written name = value. sysctl -w sets it until the next reboot. A file in /etc/sysctl.d/ sets it permanently.

This question uses no kubectl at all. It is Linux work on one machine.

keys: the 4 parameters (copy them, do not retype)

dpkg -i /root/cri-dockerd.deb

vim /etc/sysctl.d/k8s.conf                   # paste the parameters from the question

sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward                   # = 1

Target time: 4 minutes.

story.broken: A new table (node) has no stove adapter: cri-dockerd isn't installed or running.
story.fix: dpkg -i cri-dockerd.deb, systemctl enable --now cri-docker, and set the kernel settings.

questions.title: Install a CNI (network plug-in)

pic.say: Install the network plug-in so pods get IPs.

questions.words:
• CNI = the network plug-in. It gives every pod an IP address and lets pods talk to each other. Without it, nodes stay NotReady and pods stay Pending.
  • Flannel and Calico = two common CNIs. Flannel does NOT enforce NetworkPolicy. Calico does. This one fact decides the question.
  • Pod CIDR = the IP range the cluster uses for pods, for example 10.244.0.0/16. The CNI must be told the same range.
questions.setupNote: A running playground already has a CNI, so this cannot be built there. Learn the steps. Practise them in killer.sh.
questions.question: The cluster has no CNI installed. Install ONE of the following, from the given manifest:
questions.meaning: Pick the right one, then install it. "Must support NetworkPolicy" means Calico.

steps.title: Step 1. Install the Calico operator
steps.html:
k create -f <tigera-operator URL from the question>

Use create, not apply. The file is very large and apply refuses it with metadata.annotations: Too long.

flow.t: k create -f <tigera-operator URL from the question>

flow.h: Use create, not apply. The file is very large and apply refuses it with metadata.annotations: Too long.

steps.title: Step 2. Find the cluster's pod IP range
steps.html:
k -n kube-system get pod -l component=kube-controller-manager -o yaml | grep cluster-cidr

You see for example - --cluster-cidr=10.244.0.0/16. Write it down.

flow.t: k -n kube-system get pod -l component=kube-controller-manager -o yaml | grep cluster-cidr

flow.h: You see for example - --cluster-cidr=10.244.0.0/16. Write it down.

steps.title: Step 3. Download the settings file and put the range in
steps.html:
curl -LO <custom-resources URL from the question>
vim custom-resources.yaml

Type /cidr and press Enter. Change the value to the range from step 2:

      cidr: 10.244.0.0/16

Save with Esc, :wq.

flow.h: Type /cidr and press Enter. Change the value to the range from step 2:
Save with Esc, :wq.

steps.title: Step 4. Apply it
steps.html: k apply -f custom-resources.yaml

steps.title: Closing routine
steps.html:
Give it 1 to 2 minutes.

k get pods -A | grep -i -E "calico|tigera"
k get nodes

You want the calico pods Running and all nodes Ready.

exit          # exam only

flow.h: Give it 1 to 2 minutes.
You want the calico pods Running and all nodes Ready.

You see Cause Fix
calico pods Running but other pods get no IP / stay ContainerCreating the cidr: in the file is not the cluster's range fix the file, k apply -f custom-resources.yaml again
Too long: must have at most 262144 bytes you used apply for the operator k create -f ...
the question does NOT mention NetworkPolicy either CNI is fine Flannel is one command: k apply -f <flannel URL>

k create -f <tigera-operator URL>
k -n kube-system get pod -l component=kube-controller-manager -o yaml | grep cluster-cidr
curl -LO <custom-resources URL> ; vim custom-resources.yaml      # cidr: <that range>
k apply -f custom-resources.yaml
k get nodes                                                       # Ready

questions.title: kubeadm upgrade

pic.say: Upgrade the cluster one node at a time.

questions.words:
• kubeadm = the tool that installed the cluster. It also upgrades it.
  • Three programs are upgraded on each machine: kubeadm (the tool), kubelet (the node agent), kubectl (the command line).
  • drain / uncordon = drain moves the pods off a node and closes it for new pods. uncordon opens it again. You drain before the upgrade and uncordon after.

Do not memorise the commands. Follow the docs page line by line. Memorise only the order:

drain → new kubeadm → kubeadm upgrade → new kubelet + kubectl → restart kubelet → uncordon
questions.setupNote: A normal playground is already on the newest version. Use a Killercoda scenario named "cluster upgrade" (search "CKA upgrade"), or killer.sh.
questions.question: Upgrade the control plane node to Kubernetes `1.35.2`. Then upgrade the worker node `node01` to the same version. Drain each node before upgrading it and make it schedulable again afterwards.
questions.meaning: Do the same 6-step routine twice: once on the control plane, once on the worker. Only ONE command differs between the two (step 3).

steps.title: Closing routine
steps.html:
k get nodes

You want VERSION v1.35.2 on both nodes, STATUS Ready, and NO SchedulingDisabled.

exit          # exam only

flow.h: You want VERSION v1.35.2 on both nodes, STATUS Ready, and NO SchedulingDisabled.

questions.wrong:
You see Cause Fix
SchedulingDisabled next to a node you forgot uncordon k uncordon <node>
k drain refuses: "cannot delete Pods with local storage" missing flag add --delete-emptydir-data
k drain refuses: pods "not managed by a controller" a bare pod is on the node add --force
Version '1.35.2' not found you need the full text copy it from apt-cache madison kubeadm
VERSION still old after the upgrade the kubelet was not restarted systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart kubelet
localhost:8080 was refused you ran k drain / k uncordon on node01 exit first
questions.mug:
k drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data        # from the control plane
apt: unhold → install kubeadm=<ver> → hold
kubeadm upgrade apply v<ver>          # control plane          |  kubeadm upgrade node     # worker
apt: unhold → install kubelet=<ver> kubectl=<ver> → hold
systemctl daemon-reload ; systemctl restart kubelet
k uncordon <node>                                                # from the control plane

Target time: 12 minutes. Do this question late in the exam.

story.broken: The kitchen runs an old version; every table must move to 1.35.2, one at a time.
story.fix: Drain, kubeadm upgrade, upgrade kubelet, restart, uncordon — control plane first, then node01.

questions.title: etcd backup and restore (lower priority)

pic.say: Back up the cluster database and restore it.

questions.words:
• etcd = the database where the cluster stores every object. It runs as a static pod from /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml.
  • Snapshot = a backup file of that database. Made with etcdctl snapshot save.
  • Restore = unpack a snapshot into a NEW folder, then tell etcd to use that folder.

etcd only accepts connections that show three certificate files. Their paths are written in etcd.yaml.
questions.setup: rm -f /opt/etcd-backup.db ; rm -rf /var/lib/etcd-restored ; clear
questions.setupNote: Nothing to build. Run it on the control plane of any playground. (Backup only is safe. The restore changes the cluster; do it in a playground you can throw away.)
questions.question: 1. Create a snapshot of etcd, which runs at `https://127.0.0.1:2379`, and save it to `/opt/etcd-backup.db`.
questions.meaning: Part 1 is one long command. Part 2 is one command plus a 1-line change in etcd.yaml.

steps.title: Step 1. Get the command from the docs
steps.html:
1. Open https://kubernetes.io/docs
  2. Search: etcd backup
  3. Click: "Operating etcd clusters for Kubernetes" (direct link: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/configure-upgrade-etcd/ )
  4. Go to the heading "Backing up an etcd cluster" → "Snapshot using etcdctl options". Copy the command that has --cacert, --cert and --key.

flow.h: 1. Open https://kubernetes.io/docs 2. Search: etcd backup 3. Click: "Operating etcd clusters for Kubernetes" (direct link: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/configure-upgrade-etcd/ ) 4. Go to the heading "Backing up an etcd cluster" → "Snapshot using etcdctl options". Copy the command that has --cacert, --cert and --key.

steps.title: Step 2. Find the three certificate paths
steps.html:
grep -E "trusted-ca-file|cert-file|key-file" /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml

Use the three lines WITHOUT the word peer:

Line in etcd.yaml Flag for etcdctl Usual value
--trusted-ca-file= --cacert= /etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt
--cert-file= --cert= /etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt
--key-file= --key= /etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key

flow.h: Use the three lines WITHOUT the word peer: | Line in etcd.yaml | Flag for etcdctl | Usual value | |---|---|---| | --trusted-ca-file= | --cacert= | /etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt | | --cert-file= | --cert= | /etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt | | --key-file= | --key= | /etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key |

steps.title: Step 3. Take the snapshot
steps.html:
etcdctl snapshot save /opt/etcd-backup.db \
  --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 \
  --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt \
  --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt \
  --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key

You want Snapshot saved at /opt/etcd-backup.db.

If the question only asks for a backup, you are finished: ls -l /opt/etcd-backup.db.

flow.h: You want Snapshot saved at /opt/etcd-backup.db. If the question only asks for a backup, you are finished: ls -l /opt/etcd-backup.db.

steps.title: Step 4. Restore into a new folder
steps.html:
etcdutl snapshot restore /opt/etcd-backup.db --data-dir=/var/lib/etcd-restored

(If etcdutl is not installed, the same line with etcdctl works.) No certificates needed: this only unpacks a file.

flow.h: (If etcdutl is not installed, the same line with etcdctl works.) No certificates needed: this only unpacks a file.

steps.title: Step 5. Tell etcd to use the new folder
steps.html:
cp /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml /root/etcd.yaml.bak
vim /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml

Press G to jump to the end of the file. You see:

  volumes:
  - hostPath:
      path: /etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd
      type: DirectoryOrCreate
    name: etcd-certs
  - hostPath:
      path: /var/lib/etcd
      type: DirectoryOrCreate
    name: etcd-data

Change ONE line: in the block named etcd-data, change

Before After
path: /var/lib/etcd path: /var/lib/etcd-restored

Save with Esc, :wq.

Why only this line: hostPath is the folder on the machine. It is shown INSIDE the etcd container at /var/lib/etcd (that is the mountPath). etcd reads /var/lib/etcd inside the container (that is --data-dir). By changing only the hostPath, etcd keeps reading the same place, but that place now shows the restored folder. Leave --data-dir and mountPath alone.

Check:

grep -n "etcd-restored" /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml

You want exactly 1 line.

flow.h: Press G to jump to the end of the file. You see:

flow.t:
volumes:
  - hostPath:
      path: /etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd
      type: DirectoryOrCreate
    name: etcd-certs
  - hostPath:
      path: /var/lib/etcd
      type: DirectoryOrCreate
    name: etcd-data

flow.h: Change ONE line: in the block named etcd-data, change | Before | After | |---|---| | path: /var/lib/etcd | path: /var/lib/etcd-restored | Save with Esc, :wq. Why only this line: hostPath is the folder on the machine. It is shown INSIDE the etcd container at /var/lib/etcd (that is the mountPath). etcd reads /var/lib/etcd inside the container (that is --data-dir). By changing only the hostPath, etcd keeps reading the same place, but that place now shows the restored folder. Leave --data-dir and mountPath alone. Check:
You want exactly 1 line.

steps.title: Closing routine
steps.html:
The kubelet restarts etcd by itself. kubectl does not answer for up to 60 seconds. That is normal.

k get nodes
k get pods -n kube-system | grep etcd        # 1/1 Running
exit          # exam only

flow.h: The kubelet restarts etcd by itself. kubectl does not answer for up to 60 seconds. That is normal.

flow.t: k get pods -n kube-system | grep etcd

questions.wrong:
You see Cause Fix
snapshot save hangs or says context deadline exceeded a certificate path or the endpoint is wrong compare with step 2
kubectl does not come back after 2 minutes a typo in etcd.yaml `crictl ps -a
data-dir ... not empty on restore the target folder already exists choose a new folder name or rm -rf it first
questions.mug:
grep -E "trusted-ca-file|cert-file|key-file" /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml
etcdctl snapshot save /opt/etcd-backup.db --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=... --cert=... --key=...
etcdutl snapshot restore /opt/etcd-backup.db --data-dir=/var/lib/etcd-restored
vim /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml      # hostPath path: /var/lib/etcd-restored
k get nodes                                  # wait up to 60 s

Target time: 10 minutes.

story.broken: The order book (etcd) has no copy; if it's lost, every order is gone.
story.fix: etcdctl snapshot save with the certs; later, snapshot restore into a new data dir.

questions.title: NodePort

pic.say: Open the app on every node's port with a NodePort Service.

questions.words:
• containerPort = a line in the pod template that states which port the container listens on.
  • NodePort Service = a Service that also opens a port on every node. Three numbers are involved:
    • port = the Service's own port
    • targetPort = the container's port
    • nodePort = the port on every node (30000 to 32767)
  • k expose = the command that creates a Service for a Deployment. It copies the Deployment's labels into the selector, so the selector is always right.
questions.setup:
k delete ns web --ignore-not-found
k create ns web
k create deploy np --image=nginx:1.27 -n web
questions.question: In namespace `web`:
questions.meaning: Two jobs. Add two lines to the Deployment. Create a Service, then set its node port to a fixed number (Kubernetes picks a random one otherwise).

steps.title: Step 1. Add the container port to the Deployment
steps.html:
k edit deploy np -n web

Type /image: and press Enter. You see:

      containers:
      - image: nginx:1.27
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        name: nginx

Press o (opens a new line below) and add these two lines. ports: must start in the same column as image: / name::

        ports:
        - containerPort: 80

Save with Esc, :wq. You see deployment.apps/np edited.

flow.h: Type /image: and press Enter. You see:

flow.t:
containers:
      - image: nginx:1.27
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        name: nginx

flow.h: Press o (opens a new line below) and add these two lines. ports: must start in the same column as image: / name::
Save with Esc, :wq. You see deployment.apps/np edited.

steps.title: Step 2. Create the Service
steps.html: k expose deploy np --name=np-svc --port=80 --target-port=80 --type=NodePort -n web

steps.title: Step 3. Set the node port
steps.html:
k edit svc np-svc -n web

Type /nodePort and press Enter. You see a random number:

  - nodePort: 31544
    port: 80

Change it to 30080. Save with Esc, :wq.

flow.h: Type /nodePort and press Enter. You see a random number:
Change it to 30080. Save with Esc, :wq.

steps.title: Closing routine
steps.html:
k get svc np-svc -n web

You want TYPE NodePort and PORT(S) 80:30080/TCP.

k get endpoints np-svc -n web                # an IP with :80
curl -s -m 3 node01:30080 | head -5          # the nginx page
exit          # exam only

flow.h: You want TYPE NodePort and PORT(S) 80:30080/TCP.

questions.wrong:
You see Cause Fix
after step 1 vim reopens with an error at the top wrong indentation, or a Tab character ports: lines up with name:. Spaces only.
the Service is called np you forgot --name=np-svc k delete svc np -n web, run step 2 again
provided port is not in the valid range nodePort outside 30000 to 32767 use the number from the question
curl fails but endpoints are fine you curled the wrong node name k get nodes -o wide, use a node IP
questions.mug:
k edit deploy np -n web                      # add ports: / - containerPort: 80
k expose deploy np --name=np-svc --port=80 --target-port=80 --type=NodePort -n web
k edit svc np-svc -n web                     # nodePort: 30080
k get svc np-svc -n web                      # 80:30080/TCP

story.broken: The dishes have no phone number that works from outside the restaurant.
story.fix: Name the container port, then kubectl expose as type NodePort — a number on every table.

questions.title: Ingress

pic.say: Route web traffic by host name with an Ingress.

questions.words:
• Ingress = a rule for web traffic coming into the cluster: "host X, path Y → Service Z, port N".
  • IngressClass = the name of the controller that will carry out the rule (for example nginx). An Ingress without a class is ignored.
  • pathType: Prefix = the rule matches the path and everything below it. / with Prefix matches every request.
questions.setup:
k delete ns web --ignore-not-found
k create ns web
k create deploy backend --image=nginx:1.27 -n web
k expose deploy backend --name=backend-svc --port=80 -n web
cat <<EOF | k apply -f -
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: IngressClass
metadata:
  name: nginx
spec:
  controller: k8s.io/ingress-nginx
EOF
questions.question: In namespace `web`, create an Ingress named `web-ing` that uses the existing IngressClass. Requests for host `shop.example.com` with path `/` (type Prefix) must go to service `backend-svc` on port `80`.
questions.meaning: One object, and there is a command for it. No YAML.

steps.title: Step 1. Find the class name
steps.html:
k get ingressclass

You see nginx. Write it down.

flow.h: You see nginx. Write it down.

steps.title: Step 2. Create the Ingress
steps.html:
k create ingress web-ing --class=nginx --rule="shop.example.com/*=backend-svc:80" -n web

How to read the rule: "HOST/PATH=SERVICE:PORT"

Part Meaning
shop.example.com the host
/* path /. The * makes it pathType: Prefix. Without * it becomes Exact.
backend-svc:80 Service name and Service port

flow.h: How to read the rule: "HOST/PATH=SERVICE:PORT" | Part | Meaning | |---|---| | shop.example.com | the host | | /* | path /. The * makes it pathType: Prefix. Without * it becomes Exact. | | backend-svc:80 | Service name and Service port |

steps.title: Closing routine
steps.html:
k describe ing web-ing -n web

You want:

Ingress Class:    nginx
Rules:
  Host              Path  Backends
  shop.example.com  /     backend-svc:80 (192.168.x.x:80)

The IP in brackets proves the Service name and port are right.

exit          # exam only

flow.h: You want:

flow.t:
Ingress Class:    nginx
Rules:
  Host              Path  Backends
  shop.example.com  /     backend-svc:80 (192.168.x.x:80)

flow.h: The IP in brackets proves the Service name and port are right.

questions.wrong:
You see Cause Fix
Backends shows <error: services "..." not found> the Service name or port has a typo k delete ing web-ing -n web, create again
Ingress Class: <none> you forgot --class delete and create again
the question asks for TLS with secret web-tls add it inside the rule --rule="shop.example.com/*=backend-svc:80,tls=web-tls"
the question asks for two paths repeat the flag --rule="host/api*=api-svc:80" --rule="host/*=web-svc:80"
the question asks for an annotation (for example rewrite-target) add a flag --annotation nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/rewrite-target=/
questions.mug:
k get ingressclass
k create ingress web-ing --class=nginx --rule="shop.example.com/*=backend-svc:80" -n web
k describe ing web-ing -n web

story.broken: Guests asking for shop.example.com at the street door have no sign telling them where to go.
story.fix: kubectl create ingress web-ing with rule shop.example.com/ → backend-svc:80.

questions.title: Gateway API (replace an Ingress)

pic.say: Replace an Ingress with a Gateway and an HTTPRoute.

questions.words:
• Gateway = the entry point: which port, which protocol, which hostname, which TLS certificate. It names a GatewayClass (the controller), the same way an Ingress names an IngressClass.
  • HTTPRoute = the routing rule: which host and path go to which Service and port. It points to its Gateway with parentRefs.
  • Together they do what ONE Ingress did. An Ingress → Gateway migration means: read the values out of the Ingress, write them into these two objects.
questions.setup:
k apply -f https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/download/v1.2.1/standard-install.yaml
k delete ns web --ignore-not-found
k create ns web
k create deploy backend --image=nginx:1.27 -n web
k expose deploy backend --name=backend-svc --port=80 -n web
openssl req -x509 -nodes -newkey rsa:2048 -days 30 -subj "/CN=shop.example.com" -keyout /tmp/t.key -out /tmp/t.crt 2>/dev/null
k create secret tls web-tls --cert=/tmp/t.crt --key=/tmp/t.key -n web
cat <<EOF | k apply -f -
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: GatewayClass
metadata:
  name: nginx
spec:
  controllerName: gateway.nginx.org/nginx-gateway-controller
EOF
k create ingress web-ing --class=nginx --rule="shop.example.com/*=backend-svc:80,tls=web-tls" -n web
questions.setupNote: (There is no real gateway controller in the playground, so traffic will not flow. You practise creating the objects correctly. That is what the exam grades.)
questions.question: In namespace `web`, an Ingress named `web-ing` exposes an application over HTTPS. Migrate it to the Gateway API:
questions.meaning: The question does not give you the values. They are inside the existing Ingress. Read 5 values from it, put them into two new objects.

steps.title: Step 1. Read the 5 values
steps.html:
k get ing web-ing -n web -o yaml
k get gatewayclass

In the Ingress YAML, find and write down:

# Value Where in the Ingress Here
1 hostname spec.rules[].host shop.example.com
2 TLS secret spec.tls[].secretName web-tls
3 path spec.rules[].http.paths[].path /
4 Service name ...backend.service.name backend-svc
5 Service port ...backend.service.port.number 80

And from k get gatewayclass: the class name → nginx.

flow.t: k get ing web-ing -n web -o yaml

flow.h: In the Ingress YAML, find and write down: | # | Value | Where in the Ingress | Here | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | hostname | spec.rules[].host | shop.example.com | | 2 | TLS secret | spec.tls[].secretName | web-tls | | 3 | path | spec.rules[].http.paths[].path | / | | 4 | Service name | ...backend.service.name | backend-svc | | 5 | Service port | ...backend.service.port.number | 80 | And from k get gatewayclass: the class name → nginx.

steps.title: Step 2. Get the text from the docs
steps.html:
1. Open https://kubernetes.io/docs
  2. Search: gateway api
  3. Click: "Gateway API" (direct link: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/gateway/ )
  4. Copy the example under the heading "Gateway", and the example under the heading "HTTPRoute".

This is what you copied (Gateway):

apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: example-gateway
spec:
  gatewayClassName: example-class
  listeners:
  - name: http
    protocol: HTTP
    port: 80

This is what you copied (HTTPRoute):

apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: example-httproute
spec:
  parentRefs:
  - name: example-gateway
  hostnames:
  - "www.example.com"
  rules:
  - matches:
    - path:
        type: PathPrefix
        value: /login
    backendRefs:
    - name: example-svc
      port: 8080

flow.h: 1. Open https://kubernetes.io/docs 2. Search: gateway api 3. Click: "Gateway API" (direct link: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/gateway/ ) 4. Copy the example under the heading "Gateway", and the example under the heading "HTTPRoute". This is what you copied (Gateway):

flow.t:

kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: example-gateway
spec:
  gatewayClassName: example-class

flow.h: This is what you copied (HTTPRoute):

flow.t:
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: example-httproute
spec:
  parentRefs:
  - name: example-gateway
  hostnames:
  - "www.example.com"
  rules:
  - matches:
    - path:
        type: PathPrefix
        value: /login
    backendRefs:
    - name: example-svc
      port: 8080

steps.title: Step 3. The Gateway
steps.html:
vim gw.yaml

Paste the Gateway example.

# The docs say You change it to Why
1 name: example-gateway name: web-gw from the question
2 (no namespace line) add namespace: web under name: from the question
3 gatewayClassName: example-class gatewayClassName: nginx the existing class (step 1)
4 - name: http - name: https just a label for the listener
5 protocol: HTTP protocol: HTTPS the Ingress used TLS
6 port: 80 port: 443 the HTTPS port
7 (not in the example) add hostname: and the tls: block, see below value 1 and value 2

The tls: block is NOT in the docs example. Memorise these 4 lines, or get them with k explain gateway.spec.listeners.tls:

    tls:
      mode: Terminate
      certificateRefs:
      - name: web-tls

The finished file:

apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: web-gw
  namespace: web
spec:
  gatewayClassName: nginx
  listeners:
  - name: https
    protocol: HTTPS
    port: 443
    hostname: shop.example.com
    tls:
      mode: Terminate
      certificateRefs:
      - name: web-tls

Save, then:

k apply -f gw.yaml

questions.title: NetworkPolicy: allow one app to reach another

pic.say: Allow only one app to reach another.

questions.words:
• podSelector at the top of the policy = the pods being protected (the destination).
  • ingress → from = who may send traffic to them (the source).
  • AND vs OR inside from: each - starts a new, separate source (OR). Two selectors under the SAME - must both be true (AND).
  - from:                                   - from:
    - namespaceSelector: ...                  - namespaceSelector: ...
      podSelector: ...                        - podSelector: ...
  ONE dash = namespace AND pod              TWO dashes = namespace OR pod  (allows much more)
questions.setup:
k delete ns prod --ignore-not-found
k create ns prod
k run db --image=nginx:1.27 -n prod --labels=app=db
k run api --image=busybox:1.36 -n prod --labels=app=api -- sleep 3600
k run other --image=busybox:1.36 -n prod --labels=app=other -- sleep 3600
k expose pod db --name=db-svc --port=80 -n prod
questions.setupNote: (nginx on port 80 plays the role of the database here.)
questions.question: In namespace `prod`, create a NetworkPolicy named `db-policy`. Pods with label `app=db` must accept incoming traffic ONLY from pods with label `app=api` in the same namespace, and only on TCP port `80`.
questions.meaning:
The same three blanks as in question 10:

Blank Value
WHO is protected app=db
WHO may come in app=api
WHICH port TCP 80

steps.title: Step 1. Check that the labels are real
steps.html:
k get pods -n prod --show-labels

You see app=db, app=api, app=other. They match the question.

  2. Under "The NetworkPolicy resource", copy the example box. (It is the same box as in question 10.)

questions.title: Default deny, but keep DNS

pic.say: Block everything but keep DNS working.

questions.words:
• Ingress (in a NetworkPolicy) = traffic coming INTO the selected pods. Egress = traffic going OUT of them.
  • Default deny = a policy that selects all pods (podSelector: {}) and allows nothing. After it, only traffic allowed by other policies passes.
  • Port 53 = the DNS port (UDP and TCP). If you block egress and do not allow port 53, pods can no longer look up any Service name.
questions.setup:
k delete ns prod --ignore-not-found
k create ns prod
k run app --image=busybox:1.36 -n prod -- sleep 3600
questions.question: In namespace `prod`, create a NetworkPolicy named `default-deny` that blocks all incoming and all outgoing traffic for every pod in the namespace. DNS lookups (port 53, UDP and TCP) must still work.
questions.meaning: One policy: select every pod, list both directions, allow nothing in, allow only port 53 out.

steps.title: Step 1. Get the policy text from the docs
steps.html:
1. Open https://kubernetes.io/docs → search network policies → click "Network Policies" (direct link: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/network-policies/ )
  2. Scroll to the heading "Default policies" → "Default deny all ingress and all egress traffic". Copy that small box.

This is what you copied:

apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny-all
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress

flow.h: 1. Open https://kubernetes.io/docs → search network policies → click "Network Policies" (direct link: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/network-policies/ ) 2. Scroll to the heading "Default policies" → "Default deny all ingress and all egress traffic". Copy that small box. This is what you copied:

flow.t:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny-all
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress

steps.title: Step 2. Paste, change 1 line, add 7 lines
steps.html:
vim deny.yaml
# The docs say You change it to Why
1 name: default-deny-all name: default-deny from the question
2 (no namespace line) add namespace: prod under name: from the question
3 (file ends after - Egress) add the egress: block below the DNS exception

The finished file:

apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny
  namespace: prod
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress
  egress:
  - ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 53

How it reads: "All pods. Both directions are restricted. Nothing may come in (no ingress: section). Going out, only port 53 is allowed."

egress: starts in the same column as policyTypes:.

Save, then:

k apply -f deny.yaml

flow.h: | # | The docs say | You change it to | Why | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | name: default-deny-all | name: default-deny | from the question | | 2 | (no namespace line) | add namespace: prod under name: | from the question | | 3 | (file ends after - Egress) | add the egress: block below | the DNS exception | The finished file:

flow.t:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny
  namespace: prod
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress
  egress:
  - ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 53

steps.title: Closing routine
steps.html:
k describe netpol default-deny -n prod

You want:

PodSelector:     <none> (Allowing the specific traffic to all pods in this namespace)
Allowing ingress traffic:    <none> (Selected pods are isolated for ingress connectivity)
Allowing egress traffic:     To Port: 53/UDP   To Port: 53/TCP
Policy Types: Ingress, Egress

Test: a name lookup works, a connection does not.

k exec app -n prod -- nslookup kubernetes.default               # an Address line
k exec app -n prod -- wget -qO- -T 3 kubernetes.default:443   # download timed out
exit          # exam only

flow.h: You want:

flow.t:
PodSelector:     <none> (Allowing the specific traffic to all pods in this namespace)
Allowing ingress traffic:    <none> (Selected pods are isolated for ingress connectivity)
Allowing egress traffic:     To Port: 53/UDP   To Port: 53/TCP
Policy Types: Ingress, Egress

flow.h: Test: a name lookup works, a connection does not.

flow.t: k exec app -n prod -- nslookup kubernetes.default
k exec app -n prod -- wget -qO- -T 3 kubernetes.default:443

k apply -f deny.yaml
k describe netpol default-deny -n prod

story.fix: Create default-deny for Ingress and Egress, but allow egress port 53 UDP/TCP to the phone book.

questions.title: TLS settings in a ConfigMap

pic.say: Change a setting inside a ConfigMap and restart the app.

questions.words:
• ConfigMap = an object that holds configuration text. A pod can mount it as a file. Here it holds the nginx config file.
  • ssl_protocols = the nginx setting that lists which TLS versions the server accepts.
  • A running pod does not re-read its config. After you change the ConfigMap you must restart the pods: k rollout restart.
questions.setup:
k delete ns nginx-static --ignore-not-found
k create ns nginx-static
k create cm nginx-config -n nginx-static --from-literal=nginx.conf="server { listen 443 ssl; ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3; }"
k create deploy nginx-static --image=nginx:1.27 -n nginx-static
questions.setupNote: This builds the objects so you can practise the three motions. (No real HTTPS server; the exam has one.)
questions.question: In namespace `nginx-static`, deployment `nginx-static` gets its configuration from ConfigMap `nginx-config`. The server currently accepts TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.3. Change the configuration so that ONLY TLSv1.3 is accepted, and make sure the running pods use the new configuration.
questions.meaning: Remove one word from one line in a ConfigMap. Then restart the Deployment so the pods pick it up.

steps.title: Step 1. Backup first
steps.html: k get cm nginx-config -n nginx-static -o yaml > /root/cm-backup.yaml

flow.t: k get cm nginx-config -n nginx-static -o yaml > /root/cm-backup.yaml

steps.title: Step 2. Change the line
steps.html:
k edit cm nginx-config -n nginx-static

Type /ssl_protocols and press Enter.

Before After
ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3; ssl_protocols TLSv1.3;

Keep the ; at the end. Save with Esc, :wq.

flow.h: Type /ssl_protocols and press Enter. | Before | After | |---|---| | ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3; | ssl_protocols TLSv1.3; | Keep the ; at the end. Save with Esc, :wq.

steps.title: Step 3. Restart the pods
steps.html:
k rollout restart deploy nginx-static -n nginx-static
k rollout status deploy nginx-static -n nginx-static

You want successfully rolled out.

flow.t: k rollout restart deploy nginx-static -n nginx-static
k rollout status deploy nginx-static -n nginx-static

flow.h: You want successfully rolled out.

steps.title: Closing routine
steps.html:
k get cm nginx-config -n nginx-static -o yaml | grep ssl_protocols
k get pods -n nginx-static                   # new pod, 1/1 Running

In the exam the question gives a test. It looks like this:

curl -k --tls-max 1.2 https://<address>      # must now FAIL
curl -k --tlsv1.3 https://<address>          # must work
exit          # exam only

questions.title: CoreDNS config

pic.say: Change CoreDNS's configuration.

questions.words:
• Corefile = the configuration text of CoreDNS. It is stored in ConfigMap coredns, namespace kube-system.
  • .:53 { ... } = the main block of the Corefile. Each line inside is a plug-in. The line kubernetes cluster.local ... is the one that answers for Service names.
  • rewrite name A B = a plug-in line: "when someone asks for name A, answer as if they asked for name B".
questions.setup:
k delete ns web --ignore-not-found
k create ns web
k create deploy backend --image=nginx:1.27 -n web
k expose deploy backend --name=backend-svc --port=80 -n web
questions.question: Configure cluster DNS so that the name `api.example.com` resolves to the service `backend-svc` in namespace `web`, for all pods in the cluster. Make sure CoreDNS uses the new configuration.
questions.meaning: Add one line to the Corefile, then restart CoreDNS. Same three motions as question 28: backup, edit, restart. A mistake here breaks DNS for the whole cluster, so the backup is not optional.

steps.title: Step 1. Backup first
steps.html: k get cm coredns -n kube-system -o yaml > /root/coredns-backup.yaml

flow.t: k get cm coredns -n kube-system -o yaml > /root/coredns-backup.yaml

steps.title: Step 2. Add the line
steps.html:
k edit cm coredns -n kube-system

You see:

  Corefile: |
    .:53 {
        errors
        health {
           lameduck 5s
        }
        ready
        kubernetes cluster.local in-addr.arpa ip6.arpa {

Put the cursor on the line ready, press o (new line below), and type, with the same indentation as ready:

        rewrite name api.example.com backend-svc.web.svc.cluster.local

Save with Esc, :wq.

flow.h: You see:
Put the cursor on the line ready, press o (new line below), and type, with the same indentation as ready:
Save with Esc, :wq.

steps.html:
k rollout restart deploy coredns -n kube-system
k rollout status deploy coredns -n kube-system

k rollout status deploy coredns -n kube-system

k get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns                # all 1/1 Running
k get svc backend-svc -n web                                 # note the CLUSTER-IP
k run t --image=busybox:1.36 --rm -it --restart=Never -- nslookup api.example.com

You want an Address: line that shows the CLUSTER-IP of backend-svc.

You see Cause Fix
coredns pods CrashLoopBackOff after the restart a typo in the Corefile k logs -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns names the line. Or put the backup back: k apply -f /root/coredns-backup.yaml, then restart again.
nslookup says NXDOMAIN the line is outside the .:53 { } block, or you did not restart check the position, restart
the question asks to forward a whole domain to another DNS server different line add a new block at the end of the Corefile: example.org:53 { forward . 10.0.0.53 } (3 lines). Docs search: customizing dns service

questions.title: DNS names across namespaces

pic.say: Reach a Service in another namespace by its full DNS name.

questions.words:
• Short name = just the Service name, for example backend-svc. It only works from a pod in the SAME namespace.
  • Full name (FQDN) = SERVICE.NAMESPACE.svc.cluster.local. It works from every namespace.
  • nslookup = asks DNS for the IP behind a name.
questions.setup:
k delete ns web --ignore-not-found
k create ns web
k create deploy backend --image=nginx:1.27 -n web
k expose deploy backend --name=backend-svc --port=80 -n web
rm -f /root/dns.txt
questions.question: From a temporary pod in namespace `default` (image `busybox:1.36`), look up the DNS name of service `backend-svc` that lives in namespace `web`. Save the output of the lookup to `/root/dns.txt`.
questions.meaning: The test pod and the Service are in different namespaces, so use the full name. Send the output into a file.

steps.title: Step 1. Build the full name
steps.html:
SERVICE   . NAMESPACE . svc.cluster.local
backend-svc . web     . svc.cluster.local     →   backend-svc.web.svc.cluster.local

steps.title: Step 2. Look it up and write the file
steps.html:
k run t --image=busybox:1.36 --rm -it --restart=Never -- nslookup backend-svc.web.svc.cluster.local > /root/dns.txt
Part Meaning
k run t --image=busybox:1.36 a temporary pod named t (in default, because there is no -n)
--rm -it --restart=Never run once, show the output, delete the pod afterwards
-- nslookup <name> the command the pod runs
> /root/dns.txt write the output into the file

flow.h: | Part | Meaning | |---|---| | k run t --image=busybox:1.36 | a temporary pod named t (in default, because there is no -n) | | --rm -it --restart=Never | run once, show the output, delete the pod afterwards | | -- nslookup <name> | the command the pod runs | | > /root/dns.txt | write the output into the file |

steps.title: Closing routine
steps.html:
cat /root/dns.txt

You want:

Name:      backend-svc.web.svc.cluster.local
Address:   10.x.x.x

Compare the address with k get svc backend-svc -n web. It is the same IP.

exit          # exam only

flow.h: You want:
Compare the address with k get svc backend-svc -n web. It is the same IP.

questions.wrong:
You see Cause Fix
NXDOMAIN / can't resolve a typo in the name, or the wrong namespace in the name build the name again from step 1
pods "t" already exists an older test pod is still there k delete pod t, run it again
the file also contains pod "t" deleted that line comes from kubectl usually accepted. To avoid it: run the pod without --rm, then k logs t > /root/dns.txt, then k delete pod t
every name fails DNS itself is broken question 11

Good to know: backend-svc.web (without the rest) also works. A pod's DNS settings are in /etc/resolv.conf: k exec <pod> -- cat /etc/resolv.conf.
questions.mug:
k run t --image=busybox:1.36 --rm -it --restart=Never -- nslookup backend-svc.web.svc.cluster.local > /root/dns.txt
cat /root/dns.txt

story.broken: A guest in one room (namespace) must look up backend-svc, which lives in room web.
story.fix: nslookup backend-svc.web.svc.cluster.local from a busybox pod; save the output to /root/dns.txt.

questions.title: Sidecar container

pic.say: Add a helper container next to the main one.

questions.words:
• Sidecar = a second container in the same pod that helps the main one (for example: reads its log file). In YAML it is written under initContainers: with restartPolicy: Always. That one line is what makes it a sidecar: it starts first and keeps running.
  • emptyDir volume = an empty folder that belongs to the pod. Every container in the pod that mounts it sees the same files.
  • volumeMounts = where a volume appears inside a container. Two containers in one pod do NOT see each other's files unless both mount the same volume.
questions.setup:
k delete ns work --ignore-not-found
k create ns work
k create deploy app --image=busybox:1.36 -n work -- sh -c "while true; do date >> /var/log/app.log; sleep 2; done"
questions.question: In namespace `work`, deployment `app` writes its log to `/var/log/app.log`. Add a sidecar container named `log-shipper` with image `busybox:1.36` that runs `tail -f /var/log/app.log`. Use a shared volume named `logs` mounted at `/var/log` in both containers. Do not change the existing container's image or command.
questions.meaning:
Add three things to the Deployment:

1. a volume                          (pod level)
2. a mount of it in the main container   (container level)
3. the sidecar, which also mounts it     (pod level, under initContainers)

steps.title: Step 1. Open the docs example next to you
steps.html:
1. Open https://kubernetes.io/docs → search sidecar containers → click "Sidecar Containers" (direct link: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/sidecar-containers/ )
  2. Under the heading "Example application" there is a Deployment. Its bottom half is exactly the shape you need:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: myapp
          image: alpine:latest
          command: ['sh', '-c', 'while true; do echo "logging" >> /opt/logs.txt; sleep 1; done']
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /opt
      initContainers:
        - name: logshipper
          image: alpine:latest
          restartPolicy: Always
          command: ['sh', '-c', 'tail -F /opt/logs.txt']
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /opt
      volumes:
        - name: data
          emptyDir: {}

You copy three pieces from it: the volumeMounts: block, the initContainers: block, the volumes: block.

flow.h: 1. Open https://kubernetes.io/docs → search sidecar containers → click "Sidecar Containers" (direct link: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/sidecar-containers/ ) 2. questions.title: HPA (autoscaling)

pic.say: Scale pods automatically with CPU load.

questions.words:
• HPA (HorizontalPodAutoscaler) = an object that changes the number of replicas of a Deployment automatically, based on CPU use.
  • Target 70% = "keep average CPU use at 70% of what each pod REQUESTED". So the Deployment must have a CPU request. Without one, the HPA cannot calculate anything.
  • Stabilization window = how long the HPA waits before it removes pods, so the count does not jump up and down.
questions.setup:
k delete ns shop --ignore-not-found
k create ns shop
k create deploy web --image=nginx:1.27 -n shop
k set resources deploy web -n shop --requests=cpu=100m
questions.question: In namespace `shop`, create a HorizontalPodAutoscaler named `web` for deployment `web`: minimum `2` replicas, maximum `5` replicas, target average CPU utilization `70`%. Set the scale-down stabilization window to `30` seconds.
questions.meaning: One command creates the HPA. One small edit adds the 3-line "behavior" block, because the command has no flag for it.

steps.title: Step 1. Create the HPA
steps.html:
k autoscale deploy web --min=2 --max=5 --cpu-percent=70 -n shop

The HPA gets the same name as the deployment: web. A warning that --cpu-percent is deprecated is harmless. If the flag is refused, run k autoscale --help and use the newer spelling shown there (--cpu=70%).

flow.h: The HPA gets the same name as the deployment: web. A warning that --cpu-percent is deprecated is harmless. If the flag is refused, run k autoscale --help and use the newer spelling shown there (--cpu=70%).

steps.title: Step 2. Add the stabilization window
steps.html:
k edit hpa web -n shop

Type /maxReplicas and press Enter. Press O (capital o: new line ABOVE) and type these 3 lines. behavior: starts in the same column as maxReplicas::

  behavior:
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 30

Save with Esc, :wq.

If you forget the spelling: docs search horizontal pod autoscaling → page "Horizontal Pod Autoscaling" → heading "Stabilization window". The same 3 lines are there.

flow.h: Type /maxReplicas and press Enter. Press O (capital o: new line ABOVE) and type these 3 lines. behavior: starts in the same column as maxReplicas::
Save with Esc, :wq. If you forget the spelling: docs search horizontal pod autoscaling → page "Horizontal Pod Autoscaling" → heading "Stabilization window". The same 3 lines are there.

steps.title: Closing routine
steps.html:
k get hpa -n shop

You want:

NAME   REFERENCE        TARGETS       MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS
web    Deployment/web   cpu: 0%/70%   2         5         2
k describe hpa web -n shop | grep -A3 -i behavior

You want Scale Down: Stabilization Window: 30 seconds.

exit          # exam only

flow.h: You want:

flow.t:
NAME   REFERENCE        TARGETS       MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS
web    Deployment/web   cpu: 0%/70%   2         5         2
k describe hpa web -n shop | grep -A3 -i behavior

flow.h: You want Scale Down: Stabilization Window: 30 seconds.

questions.wrong:
You see Cause Fix
TARGETS <unknown>/70% for more than a minute the deployment has no CPU request k set resources deploy web -n shop --requests=cpu=100m
TARGETS <unknown> and k top pods also fails no metrics-server in this playground nothing to fix; the exam has it
the question wants a different HPA name the command names it after the deployment add --name=<name> to step 1
the question asks for MEMORY no flag in older kubectl create with CPU, then k edit hpa and change name: cpu to name: memory
questions.mug:
k autoscale deploy web --min=2 --max=5 --cpu-percent=70 -n shop
k edit hpa web -n shop            # behavior: / scaleDown: / stabilizationWindowSeconds: 30
k get hpa -n shop

story.broken: No one adds or removes copies of the web dish when the kitchen gets busy.
story.fix: kubectl autoscale deploy web min 2 max 5 cpu 70%, then set scale-down window 30s.

questions.title: PriorityClass

pic.say: Make important pods win the fight for space.

questions.words:
• PriorityClass = an object that holds a number. A pod that names the class gets that priority. When the cluster is full, higher numbers are scheduled first, and lower ones can be evicted to make room.
  • User-defined = created by an admin. Two classes always exist and belong to Kubernetes itself: system-cluster-critical and system-node-critical. They do NOT count as user-defined.
  • priorityClassName = the line in the pod template (pod level) that names the class.
questions.setup:
k delete ns shop --ignore-not-found
k delete pc high-priority mid-prio low-prio --ignore-not-found
k create ns shop
k create deploy web --image=nginx:1.27 -n shop
k create pc mid-prio --value=1000
k create pc low-prio --value=100
questions.question: 1. Create a PriorityClass named `high-priority` whose value is exactly ONE LESS than the highest existing user-defined PriorityClass.
questions.meaning: Look at the existing numbers, ignore the two system- ones, subtract 1, create the class, add one line to the Deployment.

steps.title: Step 1. Look at the existing classes
steps.html:
k get pc

(pc = short for priorityclass. No namespace.)

NAME                      VALUE        GLOBAL-DEFAULT   AGE
low-prio                  100          false            1m
mid-prio                  1000         false            1m
system-cluster-critical   2000000000   false            5h
system-node-critical      2000001000   false            5h

Ignore both system- lines. Highest user-defined = 1000. One less = 999.

flow.h: (pc = short for priorityclass. No namespace.)
Ignore both system- lines. Highest user-defined = 1000. One less = 999.

steps.title: Step 2. Create the class
steps.html: k create pc high-priority --value=999

steps.title: Step 3. Put it on the Deployment
steps.html:
k edit deploy web -n shop

Type /containers: and press Enter. Press O (capital o: new line ABOVE) and type, starting in the same column as containers::

      priorityClassName: high-priority

Save with Esc, :wq.

One-line alternative (same result, no editor):

k patch deploy web -n shop -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"priorityClassName":"high-priority"}}}}'

flow.h: Type /containers: and press Enter. Press O (capital o: new line ABOVE) and type, starting in the same column as containers::
Save with Esc, :wq. One-line alternative (same result, no editor):

steps.title: Closing routine
steps.html:
k rollout status deploy web -n shop
k get pods -n shop -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,CLASS:.spec.priorityClassName,PRIO:.spec.priority

You want CLASS high-priority and PRIO 999.

exit          # exam only

flow.t: k rollout status deploy web -n shop

flow.h: You want CLASS high-priority and PRIO 999.

You see Cause Fix
you used 1999999999 you counted a system- class k delete pc high-priority, create again with the right value
new pods do not appear, k describe rs says no PriorityClass with name ... typo in the class name fix the line in k edit deploy
other pods got evicted after your change expected: higher priority pods may push out lower ones nothing to fix

k create pc high-priority --value=<that minus 1>
k edit deploy web -n shop                    # priorityClassName: high-priority  (above containers:)

questions.title: Share a node's resources between pods

pic.say: Split a node's CPU and memory fairly between pods.

questions.words:
• Allocatable = how much CPU and memory a node offers to pods in total.
  • Allocated (requests) = how much of that is already reserved by the pods running there.
  • Request = what one pod reserves. The scheduler only places a pod on a node if allocatable − already requested ≥ the pod's request. Ask for too much and the pod stays Pending.
questions.setup:
k delete ns shop --ignore-not-found
k create ns shop
cat <<EOF | k apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web
  namespace: shop
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web
    spec:
      nodeSelector:
        kubernetes.io/hostname: node01
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:1.27
EOF
questions.question: In namespace `shop`, deployment `web` runs `3` replicas, all on node `node01`. Set CPU and memory requests so that the three pods share the node's available resources equally. Leave roughly 10% headroom so the node stays stable. All 3 pods must be Running afterwards.
questions.meaning:
A calculation, then one command:

(allocatable − already requested) × 0.9 ÷ 3  =  request per pod

steps.title: Step 1. Take the deployment out of the calculation
steps.html:
k scale deploy web --replicas=0 -n shop

Now the node's numbers show only what OTHER pods use.

flow.h: Now the node's numbers show only what OTHER pods use.

steps.title: Step 2. Read the two numbers
steps.html:
k describe node node01 | grep -A7 "Allocatable:"
k describe node node01 | grep -A6 "Allocated resources:"

Example output:

Allocatable:
  cpu:       1
  memory:    1843756Ki
...
Allocated resources:
  Resource   Requests     Limits
  cpu        250m (25%)   0 (0%)
  memory     200Mi (11%)  ...

flow.t: k describe node node01 | grep -A6 "Allocated resources:"

flow.h: Example output:

flow.t:
Allocatable:
  cpu:       1
  memory:    1843756Ki
...
Allocated resources:
  Resource   Requests     Limits
  cpu        250m (25%)   0 (0%)
  memory     200Mi (11%)  ...

steps.title: Step 3. Calculate
steps.html:
Convert first: 1 CPU = 1000m. Memory in Ki ÷ 1024 = Mi → 1843756Ki ≈ 1800Mi.

CPU Memory
Allocatable 1000m 1800Mi
− already requested − 250m − 200Mi
= free 750m 1600Mi
× 0.9 (keep 10%) 675m 1440Mi
÷ 3 pods 225m 480Mi
round DOWN 220m 480Mi

Use YOUR numbers. Always round down.

flow.h: Convert first: 1 CPU = 1000m. Memory in Ki ÷ 1024 = Mi → 1843756Ki ≈ 1800Mi. | | CPU | Memory | |---|---|---| | Allocatable | 1000m | 1800Mi | | − already requested | − 250m | − 200Mi | | = free | 750m | 1600Mi | | × 0.9 (keep 10%) | 675m | 1440Mi | | ÷ 3 pods | 225m | 480Mi | | round DOWN | 220m | 480Mi | Use YOUR numbers. Always round down.

steps.title: Step 4. Set the requests and bring the pods back
steps.html:
k set resources deploy web -n shop --requests=cpu=220m,memory=480Mi
k scale deploy web --replicas=3 -n shop

Only if the question also asks for limits: add --limits=cpu=220m,memory=480Mi.

flow.t: k set resources deploy web -n shop --requests=cpu=220m,memory=480Mi

flow.h: Only if the question also asks for limits: add --limits=cpu=220m,memory=480Mi.

steps.title: Closing routine
steps.html:
k get pods -n shop -o wide

You want 3 pods, all Running, all on node01.

k describe node node01 | grep -A6 "Allocated resources:"

You want CPU and memory requests around 90%, not above 100%.

exit          # exam only

flow.h: You want 3 pods, all Running, all on node01.

flow.t: k describe node node01 | grep -A6 "Allocated resources:"

flow.h: You want CPU and memory requests around 90%, not above 100%.

You see Cause Fix
one pod Pending, Events: Insufficient cpu (or memory) the requests are a bit too big lower them by 10% and run step 4 again
the pod has init containers too they also need room k edit deploy web -n shop and give the init containers the same resources: block
the deployment has 2 containers per pod set resources applies the values to EVERY container divide by (pods × containers), or name one container: -c <name>
questions.mug:

k describe node node01 | grep -A7 "Allocatable:"
k describe node node01 | grep -A6 "Allocated resources:"
k set resources deploy web -n shop --requests=cpu=<X>m,memory=<Y>Mi      # (free × 0.9) ÷ 3, rounded down
k scale deploy web --replicas=3 -n shop      ;  k get pods -n shop

story.fix: Scale to 0, split free CPU/memory (keep ~10% spare) by 3, set requests, scale back to 3.

questions.title: ConfigMap and Secret in a pod

pic.say: Feed settings and passwords into a pod.

questions.words:
• ConfigMap = holds plain settings as KEY=VALUE. Secret = the same, for sensitive values (passwords).
  • As environment variables = every key becomes a variable inside the container. Written with envFrom: at CONTAINER level.
  • As files (a volume) = every key becomes a file in a folder inside the container; the file's content is the value. Needs two blocks: volumes: at POD level and volumeMounts: at CONTAINER level, linked by the same name:.
questions.setup:
k delete ns app --ignore-not-found
k create ns app
questions.question: In namespace `app`:
questions.meaning: Two one-line commands, then a pod YAML to which you add two blocks: envFrom (for the ConfigMap) and volumes + volumeMounts (for the Secret).

steps.title: Step 1. Create the ConfigMap and the Secret
steps.html:
k create cm app-cfg --from-literal=LOG_LEVEL=debug -n app
k create secret generic db-sec --from-literal=password=s3cret -n app

flow.t: k create secret generic db-sec --from-literal=password=s3cret -n app

steps.title: Step 2. Generate the pod YAML (no typing)
steps.html:
k run api --image=nginx:1.27 -n app --dry-run=client -o yaml > pod.yaml
vim pod.yaml

--dry-run=client -o yaml = print the YAML, create nothing. You see:

spec:
  containers:
  - image: nginx:1.27
    name: api
    resources: {}
  dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst
  restartPolicy: Always

flow.t: k run api --image=nginx:1.27 -n app --dry-run=client -o yaml > pod.yaml

flow.h: --dry-run=client -o yaml = print the YAML, create nothing. You see:

flow.t:
spec:
  containers:
  - image: nginx:1.27
    name: api
    resources: {}
  dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst
  restartPolicy: Always

steps.title: Step 3. Where to copy the two blocks from
steps.html:
Block Docs search Page Copy
envFrom configmap "Configure a Pod to Use a ConfigMap" → heading "Configure all key-value pairs in a ConfigMap as container environment variables" the 3 lines envFrom: / - configMapRef: / name:
Secret volume secret volume "Distribute Credentials Securely Using Secrets" → heading "Create a Pod that has access to the secret data through a Volume" the volumeMounts: block and the volumes: block

flow.h: | Block | Docs search | Page | Copy | |---|---|---|---| | envFrom | configmap | "Configure a Pod to Use a ConfigMap" → heading "Configure all key-value pairs in a ConfigMap as container environment variables" | the 3 lines envFrom: / - configMapRef: / name: | | Secret volume | secret volume | "Distribute Credentials Securely Using Secrets" → heading "Create a Pod that has access to the secret data through a Volume" | the volumeMounts: block and the volumes: block |

steps.title: Step 4. Add the two blocks
steps.html:
Lines marked # ADD are new. Do not type the # ADD text.

spec:
  containers:
  - image: nginx:1.27
    name: api
    resources: {}
    envFrom:                       # ADD  (container level: same column as "image:")
    - configMapRef:                # ADD
        name: app-cfg              # ADD
    volumeMounts:                  # ADD  (container level)
    - name: db                     # ADD
      mountPath: /etc/db           # ADD
  volumes:                         # ADD  (pod level: same column as "containers:")
  - name: db                       # ADD
    secret:                        # ADD
      secretName: db-sec           # ADD
  dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst
  restartPolicy: Always

How it reads:

  • envFrom → "take every key of ConfigMap app-cfg and make it an environment variable"
  • volumes → "this pod has storage called db, and its content is Secret db-sec"
  • volumeMounts → "show storage db inside the container at /etc/db"

db is just a linking name you choose. It must be the same in both blocks.

Save with Esc, :wq. Then:

k apply -f pod.yaml

flow.h: Lines marked # ADD are new. Do not type the # ADD text.

steps.title: Closing routine
steps.html:
k get pod api -n app                         # 1/1 Running
k exec api -n app -- env | grep LOG_LEVEL    # LOG_LEVEL=debug
k exec api -n app -- ls /etc/db              # password
k exec api -n app -- cat /etc/db/password    # s3cret
exit          # exam only

flow.t: k exec api -n app -- env | grep LOG_LEVEL

questions.wrong:
You see Cause Fix
STATUS CreateContainerConfigError the ConfigMap or Secret name in the pod does not exist k describe pod api -n app names it. k delete pod api -n app, fix pod.yaml, apply again.
error validating data: unknown field "volumes" volumes: is indented under the container move it to pod level (same column as containers:)
unknown field "secretName" under configMap wrong word Secret volume uses secretName:. ConfigMap volume uses name:.
A pod cannot be changed after creation (for these fields) k delete pod api -n app, fix the file, apply again

Variants:

  • Only ONE key as a variable: use env: with valueFrom: → configMapKeyRef: (name: + key:). Same docs page, heading "Define container environment variables using ConfigMap data".
  • Secret as environment variables: envFrom: → - secretRef: → name: db-sec.
  • ConfigMap as files: volumes: → configMap: → name: app-cfg.

k create cm app-cfg --from-literal=LOG_LEVEL=debug -n app
k create secret generic db-sec --from-literal=password=s3cret -n app
k run api --image=nginx:1.27 -n app --dry-run=client -o yaml > pod.yaml
vim pod.yaml          # container: envFrom + volumeMounts      pod: volumes
k apply -f pod.yaml   ;   k exec api -n app -- env | grep LOG_LEVEL

story.broken: Dish api needs its recipe card (ConfigMap) and secret sauce (Secret), but neither exists.
story.fix: Create cm app-cfg and secret db-sec, then give them to pod api as env vars.

questions.title: Taint, toleration, nodeSelector

pic.say: Send a pod to one node, and let it past that node's taint.

questions.words:
• Taint = a mark on a NODE, written key=value:effect. With effect NoSchedule, the scheduler puts no new pod on that node, unless the pod tolerates the taint.
  • Toleration = lines in a POD that say "I accept this taint". It only ALLOWS the pod on that node. It does not send the pod there.
  • nodeSelector = lines in a pod that say "only put me on a node with this label". This is what SENDS the pod to a node.

To get a pod onto a tainted node for sure, you need both: toleration (allowed) + nodeSelector (sent).
questions.setup:
k delete pod x --ignore-not-found
k taint node node01 env=prod:NoSchedule- 2>/dev/null
k label node node01 env- 2>/dev/null
questions.question: 1. Taint node `node01` with `env=prod:NoSchedule`.
questions.meaning: Two commands on the node. Then a pod YAML with two added blocks at pod level.

steps.title: Step 1. Taint and label the node
steps.html:
k taint node node01 env=prod:NoSchedule
k label node node01 env=prod

Check:

steps.html:
Lines marked # ADD are new.

questions.wrong:
You see Cause Fix
pod Pending, Events: had untolerated taint {env: prod} key, value or effect in the toleration differ from the taint k delete pod x, fix x.yaml, apply again
pod Pending, Events: didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector the node label is missing or different k label node node01 env=prod

Related commands:

k taint node node01 env=prod:NoSchedule-     # remove a taint: same text + "-" at the end
k label node node01 env-                     # remove a label: key + "-"
k describe node <node> | grep -i taints      # see taints

questions.title: Rolling update and rollback

pic.say: Roll out a new version, then roll back.

questions.words:
• Rolling update = when you change a Deployment's image, it replaces the pods a few at a time, so the app stays available.
  • Revision = each change of the pod template creates a new numbered revision. The Deployment keeps the old ones.
  • Rollback = go back to an earlier revision: k rollout undo.
questions.setup:
k delete ns shop --ignore-not-found
k create ns shop
k create deploy web --image=nginx:1.27 --replicas=3 -n shop
questions.question: In namespace `shop`:
questions.meaning: Three commands: change the image, watch it finish, undo. Then one output into a file.

steps.title: Step 1. Find the container name
steps.html:
k get deploy web -n shop -o wide

Read the CONTAINERS column: nginx. And IMAGES: nginx:1.27.

flow.t: k get deploy web -n shop -o wide

flow.h: Read the CONTAINERS column: nginx. And IMAGES: nginx:1.27.

steps.title: Step 2. Update and wait
steps.html:
k set image deploy/web nginx=nginx:1.28 -n shop
k rollout status deploy/web -n shop

You want deployment "web" successfully rolled out.

flow.t: k set image deploy/web nginx=nginx:1.28 -n shop

flow.h: You want deployment "web" successfully rolled out.

steps.title: Step 3. Look at the history, then roll back
steps.html:
k rollout history deploy/web -n shop

You see revision 1 and revision 2.

k rollout undo deploy/web -n shop
k rollout status deploy/web -n shop

To go to one specific revision instead: k rollout undo deploy/web -n shop --to-revision=1

flow.h: You see revision 1 and revision 2.
To go to one specific revision instead: k rollout undo deploy/web -n shop --to-revision=1

steps.title: Step 4. Write the image into the file
steps.html:
k get deploy web -n shop -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}' > /root/image.txt

If you cannot remember the jsonpath, this is just as good: read the image with k get deploy web -n shop -o wide, then echo nginx:1.27 > /root/image.txt.

flow.h: If you cannot remember the jsonpath, this is just as good: read the image with k get deploy web -n shop -o wide, then echo nginx:1.27 > /root/image.txt.

steps.title: Closing routine
steps.html:
cat /root/image.txt                          # nginx:1.27
k get deploy web -n shop                     # 3/3
exit          # exam only

questions.wrong:
You see Cause Fix
rollout status never finishes the new image does not exist (question 1) k rollout undo deploy/web -n shop
unable to find container named ... wrong name left of = use the CONTAINERS column from step 1

Related commands:

k scale deploy web --replicas=5 -n shop
k rollout restart deploy/web -n shop         # restart all pods, same image
k rollout pause deploy/web -n shop           # / resume

k set image deploy/web nginx=nginx:1.28 -n shop

k rollout undo deploy/web -n shop
k get deploy web -n shop -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}' > /root/image.txt

story.fix: kubectl set image to 1.28, watch rollout status, then rollout undo to go back.

questions.title: PV + PVC + Pod (build the whole chain)

pic.say: Build the disk chain: PV → PVC → Pod.

questions.words:
• PV = a disk. It belongs to the whole cluster, so it has NO namespace.
  • PVC = a request for a disk. It lives in a namespace. Kubernetes connects it to a PV that matches.
  • Pod = uses the PVC by its name. The PVC and the pod must be in the SAME namespace.

The chain is always: Pod → PVC → PV

In question 40 one part of the chain already existed. Here nothing exists. You build all three, from right to left: first the PV, then the PVC, then the pod.
questions.setup:
k delete ns storage --ignore-not-found
k delete pv pv-data --ignore-not-found
k create ns storage
questions.setupNote:
In the real exam this is already done. Paste it once, then forget it.

(The first line can take 20 seconds. That is normal.)

What now exists: an empty namespace storage. What does NOT exist: the PV, the PVC, the pod. All three are your job.
questions.question: 1. Create a PersistentVolume named `pv-data`: capacity `1Gi`, access mode `ReadWriteOnce`, hostPath `/mnt/data`, storage class `manual`.
questions.meaning:
Pod ✗   →   PVC ✗   →   PV ✗

Make a disk. Make a request that matches the disk. Make a pod that uses the request.

Kubernetes connects a PVC to a PV by comparing three values. They are all in the question:

Value PV (the disk) PVC (the request) Rule
storageClassName manual manual must be the same
accessModes ReadWriteOnce ReadWriteOnce must be the same
size 1Gi 500Mi the disk must be big enough. 1Gi is bigger than 500Mi, so it fits.

steps.title: Step 1. Open ONE docs page. It has all three pieces.
steps.html:
There is no k create pv and no k create pvc command. So you copy.

  1. Open https://kubernetes.io/docs
  2. In the search box type: persistent volume pod
  3. Click the result named: "Configure a Pod to Use a PersistentVolume for Storage" (direct link: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tutorials/configuration/configure-persistent-volume-storage/ )

Keep this page open. You will copy three boxes from it, one per step:

Step Heading on the page Box to copy
2 "Create a PersistentVolume" pods/storage/pv-volume.yaml
3 "Create a PersistentVolumeClaim" pods/storage/pv-claim.yaml
4 "Create a Pod" pods/storage/pv-pod.yaml

flow.h: There is no k create pv and no k create pvc command. So you copy. 1. Open https://kubernetes.io/docs 2. In the search box type: persistent volume pod 3. Click the result named: "Configure a Pod to Use a PersistentVolume for Storage" (direct link: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tutorials/configuration/configure-persistent-volume-storage/ ) Keep this page open. You will copy three boxes from it, one per step: | Step | Heading on the page | Box to copy | |---|---|---| | 2 | "Create a PersistentVolume" | pods/storage/pv-volume.yaml | | 3 | "Create a PersistentVolumeClaim" | pods/storage/pv-claim.yaml | | 4 | "Create a Pod" | pods/storage/pv-pod.yaml |

steps.title: Step 2. The PV (the disk)
steps.html:
Copy the box pods/storage/pv-volume.yaml. This is what you copied:

apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: task-pv-volume
  labels:
    type: local
spec:
  storageClassName: manual
  capacity:
    storage: 10Gi
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  hostPath:
    path: "/mnt/data"
vim pv.yaml

Press i, paste. Change 2 lines, delete 2 lines:

# The docs say You change it to Why
1 name: task-pv-volume name: pv-data the name the question asks for
2 storage: 10Gi storage: 1Gi the size the question asks for
3 labels: and type: local delete both lines (dd twice) the question did not ask for labels

storageClassName: manual, ReadWriteOnce and /mnt/data already match the question. Lucky. In the exam, check each one against YOUR question.

No namespace: line. A PV has no namespace.

The finished file:

apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: pv-data
spec:
  storageClassName: manual
  capacity:
    storage: 1Gi
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  hostPath:
    path: "/mnt/data"

Save with Esc, :wq. Then:

k apply -f pv.yaml
k get pv

You want:

NAME      CAPACITY   ACCESS MODES   RECLAIM POLICY   STATUS      CLAIM   STORAGECLASS   AGE
pv-data   1Gi        RWO            Retain           Available           manual         5s

STATUS Available = the disk exists and nobody uses it yet.

Pod ✗   →   PVC ✗   →   PV ✓

steps.title: Step 3. The PVC (the request)
steps.html:
Copy the box pods/storage/pv-claim.yaml. This is what you copied:

apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: task-pv-claim
spec:
  storageClassName: manual
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 3Gi
vim pvc.yaml

Press i, paste. Change 2 lines, add 1 line:

# The docs say You change it to Why
1 name: task-pv-claim name: pvc-data the name the question asks for
2 (no namespace line) add namespace: storage under name: a PVC lives in a namespace
3 storage: 3Gi storage: 500Mi the size the question asks for

The finished file:

apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: pvc-data
  namespace: storage
spec:
  storageClassName: manual
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 500Mi

Save. Then:

k apply -f pvc.yaml
k get pvc -n storage

You want:

NAME       STATUS   VOLUME    CAPACITY   ACCESS MODES   STORAGECLASS   AGE
pvc-data   Bound    pv-data   1Gi        RWO            manual         5s

Check two columns: STATUS = Bound, VOLUME = pv-data.

CAPACITY shows 1Gi although you asked for 500Mi. That is correct. The PVC gets the WHOLE disk it was connected to. Do not try to fix it.

Do not go to step 4 until you see Bound. If the PVC is not bound, the pod will never start.

steps.title: Step 4. The pod
steps.html:
Copy the box pods/storage/pv-pod.yaml. This is what you copied:

apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: task-pv-pod
spec:
  volumes:
    - name: task-pv-storage
      persistentVolumeClaim:
        claimName: task-pv-claim
  containers:
    - name: task-pv-container
      image: nginx
      ports:
        - containerPort: 80
          name: "http-server"
      volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: "/usr/share/nginx/html"
          name: task-pv-storage
vim pod.yaml

Press i, paste. Change 3 lines, add 1 line:

# The docs say You change it to Why
1 name: task-pv-pod name: web-store the name the question asks for
2 (no namespace line) add namespace: storage under name: must be the same namespace as the PVC
3 claimName: task-pv-claim claimName: pvc-data the NAME of the PVC from step 3
4 image: nginx image: nginx:1.27 the image the question asks for

mountPath: "/usr/share/nginx/html" already matches. In the exam, check it against YOUR question.

Leave everything else alone. In particular, task-pv-storage appears twice (under volumes and under volumeMounts). That is just a label that links the two blocks. It must be the same in both places, so do not touch it.

How the pod file reads, in plain words:

  • volumes: = "this pod has a disk, and it comes from the PVC called pvc-data"
  • volumeMounts: = "show that disk inside the container at the folder /usr/share/nginx/html"

Save. Then:

k apply -f pod.yaml

You see Cause Fix
PVC Pending class or access mode differ between pv.yaml and pvc.yaml, or the PVC asks for MORE than the PV has k describe pvc pvc-data -n storage, read Events. k delete pvc pvc-data -n storage, fix the file, apply again.
