questions.title: StorageClass (create one and make it the default)

pic.say: Create a StorageClass and make it the default.

questions.words:
• StorageClass = a template. When a PVC asks for a disk and no PV exists, Kubernetes uses the template to CREATE a new PV automatically.
  • Provisioner = the program that actually makes the disk. It is just a name inside the StorageClass. You copy it from the question.
  • Default StorageClass = the template used when a PVC does not name any class. It shows as (default) in k get sc.

You already met the default class in question 40: it is the thing that silently creates a new empty disk when a PVC forgets storageClassName.

One more setting you will be asked for:

volumeBindingMode Meaning
Immediate create the disk the moment the PVC appears
WaitForFirstConsumer wait until a pod actually uses the PVC, then create the disk
questions.setup:
k delete sc fast standard --ignore-not-found
k patch sc local-path -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class":"false"}}}' 2>/dev/null
cat <<EOF | k apply -f -
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: standard
  annotations:
    storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class: "true"
provisioner: rancher.io/local-path
volumeBindingMode: Immediate
EOF
questions.setupNote:
In the real exam this is already done. Paste it once, then forget it.

What now exists: one default StorageClass called standard. What does NOT exist: a class called fast. That is your job.
questions.question: 1. Create a StorageClass named `fast` with provisioner `rancher.io/local-path` and volume binding mode `WaitForFirstConsumer`.
questions.meaning:
Three small jobs:

1. make a new template called fast
2. put the "default" mark on fast
3. take the "default" mark OFF the old one

The "default" mark is an annotation (a note on the object) with this exact text: storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class: "true" You never type it. You copy it from the docs.

steps.title: Step 1. Look at what exists
steps.html:
k get sc

You see something like:

NAME                 PROVISIONER             RECLAIMPOLICY   VOLUMEBINDINGMODE   ALLOWVOLUMEEXPANSION   AGE
local-path           rancher.io/local-path   Delete          WaitForFirstConsumer   false               2h
standard (default)   rancher.io/local-path   Delete          Immediate              false               10s

Read one thing: which name has (default) next to it. Here: standard. Write it down. You need it in step 5.

(sc is short for storageclass. A StorageClass has no namespace, so there is no -n.)

flow.h: You see something like:

flow.t:
NAME                 PROVISIONER             RECLAIMPOLICY   VOLUMEBINDINGMODE   ALLOWVOLUMEEXPANSION   AGE
local-path           rancher.io/local-path   Delete          WaitForFirstConsumer   false               2h
standard (default)   rancher.io/local-path   Delete          Immediate              false               10s

flow.h: Read one thing: which name has (default) next to it. Here: standard. Write it down. You need it in step 5. (sc is short for storageclass. A StorageClass has no namespace, so there is no -n.)

steps.title: Step 2. Get the StorageClass text from the docs
steps.html:
There is no k create storageclass command. So you copy.

  1. Open https://kubernetes.io/docs
  2. In the search box type: storage classes
  3. Click the result named: "Storage Classes" (direct link: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/storage-classes/ )
  4. Near the top, under the heading "StorageClass objects", find the sentence "Here's an example of a StorageClass:"
  5. Copy the box right below it.

This is what you copied:

apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: low-latency
  annotations:
    storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class: "false"
provisioner: csi-driver.example-vendor.example
reclaimPolicy: Retain # default value is Delete
allowVolumeExpansion: true
mountOptions:
  - discard # this might enable UNMAP / TRIM at the block storage layer
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
parameters:
  guaranteedReadWriteLatency: "true" # provider-specific

Good news: the long annotation is already in there. So is volumeBindingMode.

Press i, paste.

Change 3 lines:

questions.title: Reuse an existing PV (the MariaDB question)

pic.say: Reconnect an app to its old disk without losing data.

questions.words:
• PV = a disk. It exists in the cluster. Here it holds the database files.
  • PVC = a request for a disk. A pod cannot use a PV directly. A pod uses a PVC, and Kubernetes connects the PVC to a PV.

The chain is always: Pod → PVC → PV
questions.setup:
k delete ns mariadb --ignore-not-found
k delete pv mariadb-pv --ignore-not-found
k create ns mariadb
cat <<EOF | k apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: mariadb-pv
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 250Mi
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  storageClassName: ""
  hostPath:
    path: /mnt/mariadb
EOF
cat > /root/mariadb-deploy.yaml <<EOF
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: mariadb
  namespace: mariadb
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: mariadb
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: mariadb
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: mariadb
        image: mariadb:11
        env:
        - name: MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD
          value: secret
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /var/lib/mysql
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: ""
EOF
questions.setupNote:
In the real exam this is already done. You never type this part there. Paste it once, then forget it.

What now exists: a namespace, the old disk (mariadb-pv), and the app's file (/root/mariadb-deploy.yaml). What does NOT exist: a PVC, and a running database. Those are your job.
questions.question: A MariaDB deployment in namespace `mariadb` was deleted by accident. Its PersistentVolume still exists and holds the data.
questions.meaning:
Look at the chain. Only the last part is left:

Pod ✗   →   PVC ✗   →   PV ✓

You rebuild the two missing parts, so the new database uses the OLD disk and gets its old data back.

steps.title: Step 1. Look at the old disk
steps.html:
k get pv

You see:

NAME         CAPACITY   ACCESS MODES   RECLAIM POLICY   STATUS      CLAIM   STORAGECLASS   AGE
mariadb-pv   250Mi      RWO            Retain           Available                          1m

Read four columns:

Column Value Meaning
CAPACITY 250Mi size of the disk
ACCESS MODES RWO short for ReadWriteOnce
STATUS Available free; no PVC is using it
STORAGECLASS (empty) this disk has NO class. Remember this.

Why this step matters: you never write "use disk mariadb-pv" in a PVC. You write what you need, and Kubernetes picks a disk that matches. It compares three things: class, access mode, size. So your PVC must repeat the values you just read.

flow.h: You see:

flow.t:
NAME         CAPACITY   ACCESS MODES   RECLAIM POLICY   STATUS      CLAIM   STORAGECLASS   AGE
mariadb-pv   250Mi      RWO            Retain           Available                          1m

flow.h: Read four columns: | Column | Value | Meaning | |---|---|---| | CAPACITY | 250Mi | size of the disk | | ACCESS MODES | RWO | short for ReadWriteOnce | | STATUS | Available | free; no PVC is using it | | STORAGECLASS | (empty) | this disk has NO class. Remember this. | Why this step matters: you never write "use disk mariadb-pv" in a PVC. You write what you need, and Kubernetes picks a disk that matches. It compares three things: class, access mode, size. So your PVC must repeat the values you just read.

steps.title: Step 2. Get the PVC text from the docs
steps.html:
There is no k create pvc command. So you copy from the docs. Do not type it from memory.

  1. Open https://kubernetes.io/docs
  2. In the search box type: persistent volume pod
  3. Click the result named: "Configure a Pod to Use a PersistentVolume for Storage" (direct link: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tutorials/configuration/configure-persistent-volume-storage/ )
  4. On the right side of the page, click the heading: "Create a PersistentVolumeClaim"
  5. You see a box labelled pods/storage/pv-claim.yaml. Click the copy icon at the top of that box.

This is what you copied:

apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: task-pv-claim
spec:
  storageClassName: manual
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 3Gi

flow.h: There is no k create pvc command. So you copy from the docs. Do not type it from memory. 1. Open https://kubernetes.io/docs 2. In the search box type: persistent volume pod 3. Click the result named: "Configure a Pod to Use a PersistentVolume for Storage" (direct link: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tutorials/configuration/configure-persistent-volume-storage/ ) 4. On the right side of the page, click the heading: "Create a PersistentVolumeClaim" 5. You see a box labelled pods/storage/pv-claim.yaml. Click the copy icon at the top of that box. spec:

steps.title: Step 3. Paste it into a file and change 4 things
steps.html:
vim pvc.yaml

Press i, paste, then make these 4 changes:

# The docs say You change it to Why
1 name: task-pv-claim name: mariadb the name the question asks for
2 (no namespace line) add namespace: mariadb under name: the question says namespace mariadb
3 storageClassName: manual storageClassName: "" the old disk's class is empty (step 1)
4 storage: 3Gi storage: 250Mi the size the question asks for

accessModes: ReadWriteOnce stays as it is. It already matches.

The finished file:

apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: mariadb
  namespace: mariadb
spec:
  storageClassName: ""
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 250Mi

Press Esc, type :wq, press Enter.

About change 3, the one people get wrong: do NOT delete the storageClassName line. If the line is missing, Kubernetes fills in the cluster's default class. That class then creates a brand-new EMPTY disk for you. Your PVC shows "Bound", everything looks fine, but the database has no data and you lose the points. Writing "" says "no class", which is exactly what the old disk has.

It already matches. The finished file:

  name: mariadb
  namespace: mariadb

  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce

    requests:
      storage: 250Mi

That class then creates a brand-new EMPTY disk for you. Your PVC shows "Bound", everything looks fine, but the database has no data and you lose the points. Writing "" says "no class", which is exactly what the old disk has.

steps.title: Step 4. Create the PVC and check it connected to the OLD disk
steps.html:
k apply -f pvc.yaml
k get pvc -n mariadb

You want:

NAME      STATUS   VOLUME       CAPACITY   ACCESS MODES   STORAGECLASS   AGE
mariadb   Bound    mariadb-pv   250Mi      RWO                           5s

Check two columns: STATUS = Bound, and VOLUME = mariadb-pv (the old disk's name).

The chain is now:

Pod ✗   →   PVC ✓   →   PV ✓

If something else shows up:

You see Cause Fix
STATUS Pending one of the three values does not match the disk k describe pvc mariadb -n mariadb, read Events. Then k delete pvc mariadb -n mariadb, fix pvc.yaml, apply again.
VOLUME is a long name like pvc-3f2a... you lost the storageClassName: "" line, a new empty disk was made same: delete the PVC, fix the file, apply again

(A PVC cannot be edited after creation. Delete and re-create is the normal way.)

flow.h: You want:

flow.t:
NAME      STATUS   VOLUME       CAPACITY   ACCESS MODES   STORAGECLASS   AGE
mariadb   Bound    mariadb-pv   250Mi      RWO                           5s

flow.h: Check two columns: STATUS = Bound, and VOLUME = mariadb-pv (the old disk's name). The chain is now:

If something else shows up: | You see | Cause | Fix | |---|---|---| | STATUS Pending | one of the three values does not match the disk | k describe pvc mariadb -n mariadb, read Events. Then k delete pvc mariadb -n mariadb, fix pvc.yaml, apply again. | | VOLUME is a long name like pvc-3f2a... | you lost the storageClassName: "" line, a new empty disk was made | same: delete the PVC, fix the file, apply again | (A PVC cannot be edited after creation. Delete and re-create is the normal way.)

steps.title: Step 5. Tell the app to use the PVC
steps.html:
vim /root/mariadb-deploy.yaml

Type /claimName and press Enter. The cursor jumps to the line.

Before After
claimName: "" claimName: mariadb

claimName is simply the NAME of the PVC you made in step 4. One word changes. Nothing else in this file is touched. Save with Esc, :wq.

flow.h: Type /claimName and press Enter. The cursor jumps to the line. | Before | After | |---|---| | claimName: "" | claimName: mariadb | claimName is simply the NAME of the PVC you made in step 4. One word changes. Nothing else in this file is touched. Save with Esc, :wq.

steps.title: Step 6. Start the app
steps.html: k apply -f /root/mariadb-deploy.yaml

steps.title: Closing routine
steps.html:
k get pods -n mariadb

You want 1/1 Running. The first start can take a minute while the image downloads. Run it again if you see ContainerCreating.

k get pv

You want mariadb-pv with STATUS Bound and CLAIM mariadb/mariadb. This proves the old disk is the one in use.

exit          # exam only: leave the machine before the next question

The chain is complete:

Pod ✓   →   PVC ✓   →   PV ✓

flow.h: You want 1/1 Running. The first start can take a minute while the image downloads. Run it again if you see ContainerCreating.
You want mariadb-pv with STATUS Bound and CLAIM mariadb/mariadb. This proves the old disk is the one in use.

flow.h: The chain is complete:

questions.mug:
k get pv                                   # read: size, mode, class
vim pvc.yaml                               # docs copy + 4 changes
k apply -f pvc.yaml
k get pvc -n mariadb                       # Bound + VOLUME = old PV name
vim /root/mariadb-deploy.yaml              # claimName: mariadb
k apply -f /root/mariadb-deploy.yaml
k get pods -n mariadb                      # 1/1 Running

story.fix: Write a request slip (PVC) that matches the PV, then recreate the Deployment using it.

questions.title: Node NotReady: kubelet stopped
questions.question:
ssh cka01001
The worker node node01 is reported as NotReady. Investigate the cause and bring node01 back to the Ready state. Your fix must survive a reboot of node01.
keys: fix must survive reboot (enable the service)
questions.setup:
ssh node01 'systemctl stop kubelet; systemctl disable kubelet' 2>/dev/null
sleep 45
questions.meaning: The kubelet program on node01 is switched off; turn it on and make it start automatically.

flow.h: NotReady usually means the kubelet on that node is not talking.
The kubelet runs on the node itself, not as a pod.
Shows the kubelet is stopped and will not start at boot.

steps.title: Start it and enable it at boot

flow.h: enable = survives reboot, --now = start right away.
Wait up to 30s for the node to report Ready.

questions.mug:
kubectl get nodes
ssh node01
systemctl status kubelet --no-pager
systemctl enable --now kubelet
systemctl is-enabled kubelet
exit
kubectl get nodes
kubectl get nodes
ssh node01 systemctl is-enabled kubelet

pic.say: The kubelet program on node01 is switched off; turn it on and make it start automatically.

story.broken: The cook (kubelet) at table node01 stopped and won't come back after a reboot.
story.fix: ssh node01; systemctl enable --now kubelet — the cook is back, also after reboots.

scenes.say: Welcome to Kube Foods, your restaurant company. At the top: head office. Reception takes every call. The register holds the truth. The allocation manager picks a kitchen for each new order. And the operations manager keeps everything matching the register.

Below: the branch kitchen, node zero one. Its stoves cook the dishes, the switchboard routes calls, and the branch manager, the kubelet, runs it all. Every few seconds he phones reception: branch open, all fine!
scenes.sub: kubelet = branch manager → phones "all fine" every few seconds

scenes.say: But this morning, the branch manager isn't there. No calls. After forty seconds the operations manager writes in the register: node zero one, Not Ready. And the allocation manager stops sending new orders there.
scenes.sub: No calls for 40 s → node01 NotReady → no new orders

scenes.say: Your exam task: bring node zero one back to Ready. And the fix must survive a reboot. Remember that last part.
Quick question. Why is node zero one Not Ready?

quiz.fb: Not quite. Broken stoves would hurt the dishes, but the branch would still phone in. Nobody is phoning.
Exactly! No branch manager, no phone calls, so head office marks the branch Not Ready.
Not quite. If reception were closed, nothing would work at all, not even k get nodes.

scenes.say: So drive to that branch. S S H node zero one means: open a terminal inside node zero one. Look at the prompt: it now says node zero one. You are in the kitchen.
scenes.sub: ssh node01 = drive to the branch

scenes.roster: kubelet · inactive (dead) · not on permanent roster
scenes.say: Every branch has an H R staff roster. That is system control. System control status kubelet asks: is the branch manager working? Answer: inactive, dead. He's not here.
scenes.sub: systemctl = the branch staff roster · status = is he working?

scenes.say: Easy! System control start kubelet calls him in. He's back, he phones reception, node zero one is Ready. Done? Not so fast.
scenes.sub: systemctl start = call him in… for today

scenes.say: Twist! That night the branch closes and reopens. That is a reboot. Next morning, the branch manager is missing again! Why? Start only called him in for one day. He was never put on the permanent roster.
So which command puts him on the permanent roster, and starts him right now?

quiz.fb: That's the trap we just fell into. Start is only for today.
Yes! Enable puts him on the permanent roster. Dash dash now also starts him right away.
That command doesn't exist. And kubectl only talks to head office, not to the branch roster.

scenes.say: System control enable, dash dash now, kubelet. Enable: on the permanent roster, so he comes back after every reboot. Dash dash now: start working right now.
Another night, another reboot. And this time? He's back by himself. The fix survives a reboot.
scenes.sub: Reboot again → he comes back by himself ✓

scenes.say: Now drive back with exit, and read the register with k get nodes. Node zero one: Ready. Task done!
scenes.sub: exit = drive back · k get nodes = read the register

scenes.say: Remember: Not Ready means the branch manager is missing. Drive there with S S H. Check the roster with status. And never just start him: enable dash dash now, so he survives the night.
scenes.sub: NotReady → ssh → status → enable --now → exit → get nodes

steps.do: Drive to the branch and check the branch manager
Put him on the permanent roster and start him now, then drive back

questions.title: Service has no endpoints
questions.question:
ssh cka01002
In namespace shop the Service cart does not forward traffic to the Pods of Deployment cart. Fix the Service so that it routes to the Deployment's Pods. Do not modify the Deployment.
questions.setup:
kubectl create namespace shop --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: cart, namespace: shop}
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: cart}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: cart}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - {name: nginx, image: nginx:1.27-alpine, ports: [{containerPort: 80}]}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: cart, namespace: shop}
spec:
  selector: {app: carts}
  ports: [{port: 80, targetPort: 80}]
EOF
questions.meaning: The Service is looking for the wrong Pod label; correct its selector.

flow.h: No endpoints = the Service selector matches no Pod.

flow.t: kubectl -n shop get svc cart -o wide

flow.h: One letter typo in the selector.
Point the Service at the real Pod label.

flow.t: kubectl -n shop run tmp --rm -it --restart=Never --image=busybox:1.36 -- wget -qO- -T3 cart

flow.h: A real request proves traffic flows.

questions.mug:
kubectl -n shop get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=cart
kubectl -n shop get pods --show-labels
kubectl -n shop get svc cart -o wide
kubectl -n shop patch svc cart -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"cart"}}}'
kubectl -n shop run tmp --rm -it --restart=Never --image=busybox:1.36 -- wget -qO- -T3 cart
kubectl -n shop get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=cart

pic.say: The Service is looking for the wrong Pod label; correct its selector.

story.broken: Phone number cart (Service) looks for the wrong label, so it rings no cart dishes.
story.fix: Edit the Service selector to match the cart pods' labels; leave the Deployment alone.

questions.title: Pods stuck Pending (requests too big)
questions.question:
ssh cka01003
The Pods of Deployment reporter in namespace batch stay Pending. Find the reason and fix it so that all replicas are Running. Set the memory request of the container to 128Mi. Keep the number of replicas unchanged.
questions.setup:
kubectl create namespace batch --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: reporter, namespace: batch}
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: reporter}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: reporter}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: reporter
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sh","-c","sleep 3600"]
        resources: {requests: {memory: 64Gi}}
EOF
questions.meaning: The pods ask for more memory than any node has; ask for less.

flow.h: Pending = scheduler cannot find a node.

flow.t: kubectl -n batch describe pod -l app=reporter | grep -A3 Events

flow.h: Events always tell why a pod is not scheduled.

flow.t: kubectl -n batch set resources deploy reporter --requests=memory=128Mi

flow.h: Asks for less memory so a node fits.
New pods replace the old Pending ones.

questions.mug:
kubectl -n batch get pods
kubectl -n batch describe pod -l app=reporter | grep -A3 Events
kubectl -n batch set resources deploy reporter --requests=memory=128Mi
kubectl -n batch get pods
kubectl -n batch get deploy reporter -o jsonpath="{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].resources}"
kubectl -n batch get pods

pic.say: The pods ask for more memory than any node has; ask for less.

story.broken: Reporter dishes ask for more memory than any table has, so the host can't seat them.
story.fix: kubectl set resources deploy reporter --requests=memory=128Mi — all copies get seats.

cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: api, namespace: web}

questions.title: Gateway API: migrate Ingress to Gateway + HTTPRoute
questions.question:
ssh cka01011
Migrate the existing Ingress web in namespace web-app to the Gateway API, keeping HTTPS:
- Create a Gateway named web-gateway using GatewayClass nginx, with an HTTPS listener on port 443 for hostname gateway.web.example. Use the TLS Secret web-tls already referenced by the Ingress.
- Create an HTTPRoute named web-route bound to web-gateway that sends all paths (/) for gateway.web.example to Service web on port 80.
- Delete the Ingress web when done.
keys: listener HTTPS 443, host gateway.web.example, secret web-tls
delete ingress web at the end
questions.setup:
kubectl get crd gateways.gateway.networking.k8s.io >/dev/null 2>&1 || kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/download/v1.2.1/standard-install.yaml
kubectl create namespace web-app --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
openssl req -x509 -nodes -newkey rsa:2048 -days 365 -subj "/CN=gateway.web.example" -keyout /tmp/web-tls.key -out /tmp/web-tls.crt 2>/dev/null
kubectl -n web-app create secret tls web-tls --cert=/tmp/web-tls.crt --key=/tmp/web-tls.key --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: GatewayClass
metadata: {name: nginx}
spec: {controllerName: example.net/gateway-controller}
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: web, namespace: web-app}
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: web}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: web}}
    spec:
      containers: [{name: nginx, image: nginx:1.27-alpine, ports: [{containerPort: 80}]}]
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: web, namespace: web-app}
spec: {selector: {app: web}, ports: [{port: 80, targetPort: 80}]}
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata: {name: web, namespace: web-app}
spec:
  tls: [{hosts: [gateway.web.example], secretName: web-tls}]
  rules:
  - host: gateway.web.example
    http:
      paths:
      - {path: /, pathType: Prefix, backend: {service: {name: web, port: {number: 80}}}}
EOF
questions.meaning: Rebuild the HTTPS Ingress as a Gateway (door + certificate) and an HTTPRoute (path to service). No Gateway controller runs on Killercoda, so status stays Unknown - that is fine.

steps.title: Read the Ingress you must copy

flow.t: kubectl -n web-app get ingress web -o yaml | grep -A12 "^spec"

flow.h: Host, TLS secret and backend move to the new objects.
Gateway must use an existing class.

flow.t:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata: {name: web-gateway, namespace: web-app}
spec:
  gatewayClassName: nginx
  listeners:
  - name: https
    protocol: HTTPS
    port: 443
    hostname: gateway.web.example
    tls:
      mode: Terminate
      certificateRefs:
      - {kind: Secret, name: web-tls}
EOF

flow.h: Gateway = the entry door with TLS.

flow.t:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata: {name: web-route, namespace: web-app}
spec:
  parentRefs: [{name: web-gateway}]
  hostnames: [gateway.web.example]
  rules:
  - matches: [{path: {type: PathPrefix, value: /}}]
    backendRefs: [{name: web, port: 80}]
EOF

flow.h: Route = which traffic goes to which Service.
Migration done; old object removed.

questions.title: Reuse a retained PV for MariaDB
questions.question:
ssh cka01016
A MariaDB Deployment in namespace mariadb was deleted by mistake, but its PersistentVolume mariadb-pv was kept.
- Create a PersistentVolumeClaim named mariadb in namespace mariadb: access mode ReadWriteOnce, storage 250Mi, so that it binds to the existing PV.
- Edit /root/mariadb-deploy.yaml so the Deployment uses this PVC, then apply it. Ensure the Pod is Running.
questions.setup:
kubectl create namespace mariadb --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata: {name: mariadb-pv}
spec:
  capacity: {storage: 250Mi}
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  storageClassName: ""
  hostPath: {path: /mnt/data/mariadb, type: DirectoryOrCreate}
EOF
cat <<'EOF' > /root/mariadb-deploy.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: mariadb, namespace: mariadb}
spec:
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: mariadb}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: mariadb}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: mariadb
        image: mariadb:11
        env: [{name: MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD, value: cka}]
        volumeMounts: [{name: data, mountPath: /var/lib/mysql}]
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: ""
EOF
questions.meaning: Make a storage claim that grabs the old disk, then plug it into the database deployment.

flow.h: Note size, mode and empty class.

flow.t:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: mariadb, namespace: mariadb}
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: ""
  resources: {requests: {storage: 250Mi}}
EOF

flow.h: Empty class "" stops the default class grabbing it.
Bound to the old PV = old data kept.

steps.title: Point the Deployment to the PVC

flow.h: Fill in the claim name and apply.
Database runs on the kept disk.

questions.mug:
kubectl get pv mariadb-pv
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: mariadb, namespace: mariadb}
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: ""
  resources: {requests: {storage: 250Mi}}
EOF
kubectl -n mariadb get pvc mariadb
sed -i 's/claimName: ""/claimName: mariadb/' /root/mariadb-deploy.yaml
kubectl apply -f /root/mariadb-deploy.yaml
kubectl -n mariadb get pods
kubectl -n mariadb get pvc mariadb
kubectl -n mariadb get pods

story.fix: Create PVC mariadb (RWO, 250Mi) matching the PV, then the Deployment that uses it.

questions.question:

Use the native sidecar pattern (an init container with restartPolicy: Always). Share the log directory using a volume named logs mounted at /var/log in both containers. Do not change the existing container's command.
questions.setup:
kubectl create namespace logging --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: order-app, namespace: logging}
spec:
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: order-app}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: order-app}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: [sh, -c, "while true; do echo order $(date) >> /var/log/order.log; sleep 3; done"]
EOF

flow.t: kubectl -n logging get deploy order-app -o yaml > /root/order-app.yaml

flow.t:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: order-app, namespace: logging}
spec:
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: order-app}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: order-app}}
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: log-shipper
        image: busybox:1.36
        restartPolicy: Always
        command: [sh, -c, "tail -n+1 -F /var/log/order.log"]
        volumeMounts: [{name: logs, mountPath: /var/log}]
      containers:
      - name: app

        volumeMounts: [{name: logs, mountPath: /var/log}]

      - {name: logs, emptyDir: {}}
EOF

Set up cri-dockerd on this node:
- Install /root/cri-dockerd.deb with dpkg.
- Enable and start the cri-docker socket and service so they start on boot.
- Persist these kernel settings in /etc/sysctl.d/99-cri.conf and load them now:
  net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables = 1, net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding = 1, net.ipv4.ip_forward = 1, net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 131072
- Make sure the br_netfilter module is loaded at boot (/etc/modules-load.d/cri.conf).
questions.setup: test -f /root/cri-dockerd.deb || curl -fsSLo /root/cri-dockerd.deb https://github.com/Mirantis/cri-dockerd/releases/download/v0.3.16/cri-dockerd_0.3.16.3-0.ubuntu-jammy_amd64.deb || echo "download failed - check release page"
questions.meaning: Install a runtime package, make it start at boot, and set 4 kernel network switches permanently. Docker is absent on Killercoda, so the service may fail to stay active; the rest still practises.

flow.h: Local package install.
Both units start on boot.
bridge sysctl needs this module.

flow.t:
cat <<'EOF' > /etc/sysctl.d/99-cri.conf
net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables = 1
net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding = 1
net.ipv4.ip_forward = 1
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 131072
EOF

flow.h: One setting per line.
Values active now and after reboot.

questions.mug:
dpkg -i /root/cri-dockerd.deb
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now cri-docker.socket cri-docker.service
systemctl is-enabled cri-docker.socket cri-docker.service
echo br_netfilter > /etc/modules-load.d/cri.conf
modprobe br_netfilter
cat <<'EOF' > /etc/sysctl.d/99-cri.conf
net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables = 1
net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding = 1
net.ipv4.ip_forward = 1
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 131072
EOF
sysctl --system >/dev/null
sysctl net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding net.ipv4.ip_forward net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
dpkg -s cri-dockerd | grep Status
sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
questions.docs: kubernetes.io: Container Runtimes (search: Forwarding IPv4 and letting iptables see bridged traffic)

questions.title: Gateway API: header match + weighted split
questions.question:
ssh cka03010
In namespace shop-gw a Gateway shop-gw (HTTP, port 80) and Services shop-v1 and shop-v2 exist.
Create an HTTPRoute named shop-route attached to shop-gw for hostname shop.example.com:
- Requests with header x-version: v2 go 100% to shop-v2.
- All other requests are split 80% shop-v1 and 20% shop-v2.
Both Services listen on port 80.
questions.setup:
kubectl get crd gateways.gateway.networking.k8s.io >/dev/null 2>&1 || kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/download/v1.2.1/standard-install.yaml
kubectl create namespace shop-gw --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: GatewayClass
metadata: {name: nginx}
spec: {controllerName: example.net/gateway-controller}
---
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata: {name: shop-gw, namespace: shop-gw}
spec:
  gatewayClassName: nginx
  listeners: [{name: http, protocol: HTTP, port: 80}]
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: shop-v1, namespace: shop-gw}
spec: {selector: {app: shop, v: "1"}, ports: [{port: 80}]}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: shop-v2, namespace: shop-gw}
spec: {selector: {app: shop, v: "2"}, ports: [{port: 80}]}
EOF
questions.meaning: Send testers (header v2) to version 2 and split everyone else 80/20.

flow.t: kubectl -n shop-gw get gateway shop-gw -o yaml | grep -A3 listeners

flow.h: Route will attach to this.

flow.t:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata: {name: shop-route, namespace: shop-gw}
spec:
  parentRefs: [{name: shop-gw}]
  hostnames: [shop.example.com]
  rules:
  - matches:
    - headers: [{name: x-version, value: v2}]
    backendRefs: [{name: shop-v2, port: 80}]
  - matches:
    - path: {type: PathPrefix, value: /}
    backendRefs:
    - {name: shop-v1, port: 80, weight: 80}
    - {name: shop-v2, port: 80, weight: 20}
EOF

flow.h: Header rule is more specific, so it wins.

flow.t: kubectl -n shop-gw describe httproute shop-route | grep -A20 Rules

flow.h: Both rules stored correctly.

flow.t: kubectl -n shop-gw get httproute shop-route -o yaml

questions.mug:
kubectl -n shop-gw get gateway shop-gw -o yaml | grep -A3 listeners
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata: {name: shop-route, namespace: shop-gw}
spec:
  parentRefs: [{name: shop-gw}]
  hostnames: [shop.example.com]
  rules:
  - matches:
    - headers: [{name: x-version, value: v2}]
    backendRefs: [{name: shop-v2, port: 80}]
  - matches:
    - path: {type: PathPrefix, value: /}
    backendRefs:
    - {name: shop-v1, port: 80, weight: 80}
    - {name: shop-v2, port: 80, weight: 20}
EOF
kubectl -n shop-gw describe httproute shop-route | grep -A20 Rules
kubectl -n shop-gw get httproute shop-route -o yaml
questions.docs: kubernetes.io: Gateway API; gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io: HTTP traffic splitting / header matching

pic.say: Send testers (header v2) to version 2 and split everyone else 80/20.

story.broken: Guests at gateway shop-gw have no route that checks header x-version or splits traffic.
story.fix: HTTPRoute shop-route: header x-version: v2 → shop-v2; all others split by weight.

questions.title: NetworkPolicy pick: AND vs OR trap
questions.question:
ssh cka03011
Pods labelled app=api in namespace payments must accept traffic ONLY from Pods labelled app=gateway in namespace edge, on TCP port 80. A default deny-ingress policy exists in payments.

flow.t: for f in /root/netpols-ex/*.yaml; do echo "== $f"; cat $f; done

flow.h: Look at dashes: each "-" under from is a separate OR.

flow.t: echo "a=OR (any edge pod OR any gateway pod anywhere), b=AND+port, c=no port limit, d=all edge pods+all targets -> b"

One file, no edits.

kubectl -n edge exec intruder -- wget -qO- -T2 api.payments

questions.title: HPA: CPU + memory, scaleUp and scaleDown behavior
questions.question:
ssh cka03013
Create a HorizontalPodAutoscaler named worker-hpa in namespace metrics-app for Deployment worker:
- min 2, max 6 replicas,
- target 60% average CPU utilisation AND 70% average memory utilisation,
- scale up by at most 2 Pods per 60 seconds,
- scale-down stabilization window of 120 seconds.
questions.meaning: Autoscale on CPU and memory, add at most 2 pods a minute, remove pods only after 2 calm minutes.

flow.t:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata: {name: worker-hpa, namespace: metrics-app}
spec:
  scaleTargetRef: {apiVersion: apps/v1, kind: Deployment, name: worker}
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 6
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource: {name: cpu, target: {type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 60}}
  - type: Resource
    resource: {name: memory, target: {type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 70}}
  behavior:
    scaleUp:
      policies:
      - {type: Pods, value: 2, periodSeconds: 60}
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 120
EOF

flow.h: Two metrics: HPA uses the higher demand.
<unknown> = no metrics-server; config is still right.
Without metrics the HPA may wait.

flow.t: kubectl -n metrics-app get hpa worker-hpa -o yaml | grep -A12 behavior

questions.mug:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2

metadata: {name: worker-hpa, namespace: metrics-app}
spec:
  scaleTargetRef: {apiVersion: apps/v1, kind: Deployment, name: worker}

  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource: {name: cpu, target: {type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 60}}
  - type: Resource
    resource: {name: memory, target: {type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 70}}
  behavior:
    scaleUp:
      policies:
      - {type: Pods, value: 2, periodSeconds: 60}
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 120
EOF
kubectl -n metrics-app get hpa worker-hpa
kubectl -n metrics-app get deploy worker
kubectl -n metrics-app get hpa worker-hpa -o yaml | grep -A12 behavior
questions.docs: kubernetes.io: Horizontal Pod Autoscaling (search: scaling policies behavior scaleUp)

questions.title: PriorityClass with preemption policy
questions.question:
ssh cka03014
Create a PriorityClass named critical-jobs:
- value exactly one less than the highest existing user-defined PriorityClass (ignore system-*),
- preemptionPolicy PreemptLowerPriority, not the global default,
- description "critical batch".
Patch Deployment payments-api in namespace prio to use it, and verify that the running Pods have the new priority value.
questions.setup:
kubectl create namespace prio --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata: {name: batch-low}
value: 100
---
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata: {name: team-a}
value: 3000
---
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata: {name: team-b}
value: 7000
preemptionPolicy: Never
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: payments-api, namespace: prio}
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: payments-api}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: payments-api}}
    spec:
      priorityClassName: batch-low
      containers: [{name: c, image: nginx:1.27-alpine}]
EOF
questions.meaning: Create a priority just under the top one, allowed to push others out, and give it to a deployment.

flow.h: Ignore system-* classes.

flow.t:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata: {name: critical-jobs}
value: 6999
globalDefault: false
preemptionPolicy: PreemptLowerPriority
description: "critical batch"
EOF

flow.h: YAML lets you set every field.
Replaces batch-low.

flow.t: kubectl -n prio rollout status deploy payments-api

flow.h: Priority is copied into each new pod.

flow.t: kubectl get pc critical-jobs -o yaml | grep -E "value|preemption|globalDefault"

questions.mug:
kubectl get pc --sort-by=.value -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,VALUE:.value | grep -v system-
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata: {name: critical-jobs}
value: 6999
globalDefault: false
preemptionPolicy: PreemptLowerPriority
description: "critical batch"
EOF
kubectl -n prio patch deploy payments-api -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"priorityClassName":"critical-jobs"}}}}'
kubectl -n prio rollout status deploy payments-api
kubectl -n prio get pods -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,PRIO:.spec.priority,CLASS:.spec.priorityClassName
kubectl get pc critical-jobs -o yaml | grep -E "value|preemption|globalDefault"
questions.docs: kubernetes.io: Pod Priority and Preemption (search: preemptionPolicy)

pic.say: Create a priority just under the top one, allowed to push others out, and give it to a deployment.

story.broken: Critical jobs can't push lower dishes out of the way to get a table.
story.fix: PriorityClass critical-jobs (highest minus 1, PreemptLowerPriority); patch the Deployment to use it.

questions.title: StorageClass (Retain, expandable) + StatefulSet claims
questions.question:
ssh cka03015
Create a StorageClass named retain-local: provisioner rancher.io/local-path, reclaimPolicy Retain, volumeBindingMode WaitForFirstConsumer, allowVolumeExpansion true. It must NOT be the default.
In namespace cache create a StatefulSet cache (2 replicas, image redis:7-alpine, headless Service cache) with a volumeClaimTemplate named data requesting 100Mi from retain-local, mounted at /data.
keys: sc = retain-local (Retain, WFFC, expandable, not default)
questions.setup:
kubectl get deploy -A | grep -q local-path-provisioner || kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rancher/local-path-provisioner/v0.0.30/deploy/local-path-storage.yaml
kubectl create namespace cache --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
questions.meaning: Make a storage type that keeps disks after delete, and a 2-pod database that gets one disk each.

flow.t:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata: {name: retain-local}
provisioner: rancher.io/local-path
reclaimPolicy: Retain
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
allowVolumeExpansion: true
EOF

flow.h: No default annotation = not default.
Each replica gets its own PVC.
PVs keep the Retain policy.

questions.mug:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata: {name: retain-local}
provisioner: rancher.io/local-path
reclaimPolicy: Retain
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
allowVolumeExpansion: true
EOF
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: cache, namespace: cache}
spec: {clusterIP: None, selector: {app: cache}, ports: [{port: 6379}]}
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata: {name: cache, namespace: cache}
spec:
  serviceName: cache
  replicas: 2
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: cache}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: cache}}
    spec:
      containers:
      - {name: redis, image: redis:7-alpine, volumeMounts: [{name: data, mountPath: /data}]}
  volumeClaimTemplates:
  - metadata: {name: data}
    spec:
      accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
      storageClassName: retain-local

questions.title: Re-bind a Released PV (clear claimRef)
questions.question:
ssh cka03016
The PostgreSQL data PersistentVolume pg-data-pv still holds data, but it is in Released state after its old claim was deleted.
- Make the PV available again WITHOUT deleting it or its data.
- Create PVC pg-data in namespace postgres (1Gi, ReadWriteOnce, storageClassName manual) that binds to it.
- Deploy /root/pg-deploy.yaml (already uses claim pg-data) and make sure the Pod is Running.
questions.meaning: An old disk is "locked" to a deleted claim; unlock it, claim it again, start the database.

flow.h: Released PVs never bind again by themselves.
Frees the PV; data stays on disk.
Ready for a new claim.

flow.t:
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: pg-data, namespace: postgres}
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: manual
  resources: {requests: {storage: 1Gi}}
EOF

flow.h: Class + size + mode match the PV.
Database runs on the old disk.

kubectl patch pv pg-data-pv --type=json -p='[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/claimRef"}]'

kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: pg-data, namespace: postgres}
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: manual
  resources: {requests: {storage: 1Gi}}
EOF
kubectl apply -f /root/pg-deploy.yaml
